title: Vyn
bodyText: Led by Daniel Berlin, Vyn represents a contemporary expression of southern Swedish gastronomy, where local tradition is interpreted through a forward-looking, produce-led fine dining lens.

title: AIRA
bodyText: Aira is a refined waterfront fine-dining destination where seasonal Nordic ingredients meet modern technique, elevated by truly exceptional, attentive service in a calm, design-led setting.

title: Frantzén
bodyText: Sweden’s only three-star restaurant, awarded 100 points by Falstaff. An intimate fine-dining experience, refining Swedish traditions through global influences and exceptional precision.

title: Ekstedt
bodyText: A Stockholm fine-dining landmark where all cooking is done over open fire. Nordic ingredients meet ancient and modern techniques, creating a seasonal tasting journey shaped by smoke, ash, and flame.

title: Operakällaren
bodyText: Located within Stockholm’s Royal Opera, Operakällaren is a fine dining destination led by Emanuel Tärnqvist, where refined French influences meet contemporary elegance, with an outstanding wine cellar.

title: Seafood Gastro
bodyText: Seafood Gastro focuses on sustainably sourced local seafood, with refined cooking led by Mathias Dahlgren and access to the Grand Hôtel wine cellar, served in an elegant, understated hotel setting.

title: Signum
bodyText: Set by the water, Signum is led by chef-owner Thomas Sjögren, whose tasting menu is shaped by local produce, seasonal rhythm, and a dialogue between tradition and modern craft, with a sense of place.

title: Ergo
bodyText: A contemporary French fine-dining address where chef Petter Johansson builds on classic technique with luxurious ingredients like lobster and truffle, matched with a top-tier wine list.

title: HOZE Sushiya
bodyText: Hoze is an intimate omakase sushi counter where Nordic seafood meets Japanese precision, served seat by seat in a calm, minimalist setting. With no alcohol on offer, the focus remains firmly on flavor.

title: Nour
bodyText: Guided by Sayan Isaksson, Nour delivers a highly refined dining experience in which meticulous technique meets Japanese influence, shaping dishes defined by precision, balance and aesthetic clarity.

title: Sushi Sho
bodyText: Sushi Sho is led by Carl Ishizaki and his team, serving sushi and small dishes marked by precision and restraint, using Nordic fish and seafood, counter-style, with a notably strong selection of sake.

title: Vollmers
bodyText: Vollmers works closely with the landscapes of Skåne, translating local produce into a contemporary Nordic tasting menu where tradition, precision, and subtle French influence meet.

title: Adam/Albin
bodyText: Aesthetic dishes accompany contemporary Nordic cuisine with French and Japanese influences. Currently closed, it will reopen in larger premises with a newly created menu. Points awarded prior to reopening.

title: Knystaforsen
bodyText: Set in the Halland countryside, Knystaforsen is a destination restaurant where Nicolai and Eva Tram craft terroir-driven cuisine using local ingredients shaped by fire and precision.

A long-established restaurant that has held a Michelin star for 35 years, known for classic cuisine with a modern touch and an exceptional wine list. Its wine bar offers rare pours in a relaxed setting.

title: Ett Hem
bodyText: Set inside a boutique hotel, Ett Hem offers an intimate dining experience rooted in seasonal, local produce. Thoughtful cooking, a curated wine list, and warm service create a true feeling of home.

title: Wedholms Fisk
bodyText: Wedholms Fisk specializes in top-quality fish and seafood, where classic French technique meets Swedish tradition, resulting in clean, precise cooking, supported by an extensive wine list.

title: Soyokaze
bodyText: Soyokaze offers an intimate omakase for a small number of guests, where classic sushi and sashimi meet creative, seafood-led courses, paired with expertly chosen sake and clear craftsmanship.

title: Äng
bodyText: Set along the Halland coast, Äng offers a tasting menu shaped by its surroundings, translating regional produce into a focused, contemporary dining experience, supported by a well-curated wine cellar.

title: Mathias Dahlgren Matbaren im Grand Hotel Stockholm
bodyText: Perched at the zinc-topped counter, guests watch the open kitchen in quiet motion, as this iconic food bar delivers mid-sized plates from a daily menu shaped entirely by what's in season.
venueName: Mathias Dahlgren Matbaren im Grand Hotel Stockholm

title: Pontus Frithiof La Tour
bodyText: La Tour by Pontus Frithiof sits high above the city, pairing sweeping views with a menu rooted in French tradition and modern finesse, alongside an elegant cocktail bar on the same level.

title: Ateljé Vita Duken
bodyText: Mathias Dahlgren returns to his northern hometown, opening an intimate restaurant inside the 1892 Tornhuset, where seasonal Nordic dishes draw on local ingredients and are gently cooked over glowing embers.

title: Dashi
bodyText: An acclaimed 16-seat gem, where an osusume tasting menu blends Japanese technique with Nordic produce. Take a seat at the counter, watch each dish unfold and savour excellent sake pairings.

title: AG
bodyText: AG, led by renowned chef Johan Jureskog, is a Stockholm steakhouse icon, offering expertly aged meats from Sweden and around the world, with a wide range of cuts and bold flavors.

title: PM & Vänner
bodyText: PM & Vänner draws deeply from its surroundings, with cooking rooted in local landscapes and ingredients from sea, forest, and meadow, matched by one of Sweden’s most respected and extensive wine cellars.

title: SK Mat & Människor
bodyText: Led by Stefan Karlsson, SK Mat & Människor draws on the flavors of Sweden’s west coast, with seasonal cuisine shaped by craftsmanship, restraint, and a strong sense of place, rooted in local produce.

title: Grand Soleil
bodyText: Refined yet relaxed brasserie at Grand Hôtel, blending French cuisine with other Mediterranean influences. Sea views, well-executed cooking, elegant surroundings, and polished service set the tone.

title: Hållfjället
bodyText: High in the Jämtland mountains, Hållfjället pairs mountain stillness with focused Nordic gastronomy. Wild game, lake fish and garden produce shape seasonal menus, matched by warm, attentive hospitality.

title: Persona
bodyText: Opened in 2022 by French chef Louis Cespedes and sommelier Jonatan Nyström, both alumni of Frantzén, this intimate, film-set-like room invites guests to choose a bottle from the cellar, with dishes shaped to match.

title: Bhoga
bodyText: The site of Gothenburg’s first restaurant, opened in 1669, now houses an award-winning kitchen run by Gustav Knutsson and Niclas Yngvesson. Tasting menus follow seasonal produce, paired with biodynamic wines.

title: Bobergs Matsal
bodyText: Bobergs Matsal blends over a century of heritage with refined French-Nordic cuisine. Rejuvenated under Aira’s team in a historic setting, it’s ideal for an elegant and indulgent lunch.

title: Bord
bodyText: Run by friends with fine-dining backgrounds, Bord delivers precise, produce-driven cooking from an open kitchen, with turbot highlights and an award-winning Burgundy- and Jura-focused wine list.

title: Fyr
bodyText: Chef Jacob Holmström, formerly of Gastrologik, brings refined open-fire cooking to the Swedish west coast. Local seafood takes center stage, served with quiet precision and sea views.

title: Krog Agrikultur
bodyText: Filip Fastén, who won Chef of the Year at just 24 in 2014, brings his fine dining experience to a more relaxed setting. Open since 2025, the kitchen blends French bistro style with Nordic ingredients.

title: Petri
bodyText: Petri is led by Petter Nilsson and offers a fixed seasonal menu shaped by French technique, served in a relaxed yet polished setting with thoughtful pairings, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic.

title: Etoile
bodyText: A forward-thinking restaurant where a chef-driven team explores modern gastronomy with precision and playfulness. Expect a polished yet relaxed experience that constantly challenges expectations.

title: Prins Carl
bodyText: Built in 1909 for Prince Carl of Sweden, this manor now hosts dinners beneath crystal chandeliers. A fixed five-course menu of seasonal Swedish ingredients pairs with wines from a vast cellar.

title: Verandan
bodyText: Chef’s table inside Icehotel: Up to 16 guests sit around a U-shaped counter to watch the team turn Arctic char, reindeer, and other local ingredients into a twelve-course menu that reflects the eight Sámi seasons.

title: Leijontornet
bodyText: A hedonistic dining room by Daniel Crespi, rooted in French and Italian classics, defined by luxurious ingredients, a bold signature spoon, and one of Sweden’s most impressive wine cellars.

title: Matsalen | Stockholm Stadshotell
bodyText: Led by Olle T. Cellton, the kitchen offers a changing bistro menu shaped by seasonality and local ingredients, with global touches—often drawn from southern Europe—alongside its fine-dining restaurant.

title: Åre Nature Studio
bodyText: Fredrik Karlsson built this log cabin by Lake Gevsjön, serves farm-to-table tasting menus and hunts moose and ptarmigan. With 13 seats, reservations are typically secured months in advance.

title: Gondolen
bodyText: An iconic dining room set high above the city, serving classic Swedish flavors with contemporary touches. The bar is a destination in its own right, occasionally hosting live jazz alongside sweeping panoramic views.

title: Krakas Krog
bodyText: On the island of Gotland, Krakas is a seasonal dining retreat led by sommeliers Ulrika Karlsson and Patrik Strömstedt, where local produce, open-fire cooking, and a curated wine list shape the meal.

title: Lisa Elmqvist
bodyText: A stalwart of Östermalmshallen, Lisa Elmqvist remains a seafood classic, prized for immaculate fish, generous portions and timeless dishes delivered with assured, old-school finesse.

title: Niehku Mountain Villa
bodyText: This mountain lodge follows a whole-beast approach to Arctic game and fish. A wine cellar with around 500 bottles is thoughtfully curated and located in a former engine pit within the railway roundhouse.

title: Naturaj
bodyText: Run by Johan Backéus and Birgit Malmcrona, Naturaj is guided by seasonality, sustainability and personal expression, with much of the produce drawn directly from their own garden and greenhouse.

title: Human
bodyText: Human is a refined yet personal dining room where chef-owner Martin Moses interprets modern Nordic cuisine through seasonal, local ingredients and pure, expressive flavors, guided by nature.

title: Koka
bodyText: With a strong sense of place, Koka presents seasonal tasting menus shaped by the sea and nearby farms, in an easygoing, welcoming setting suited to both celebrations and everyday dining.

title: Miyakodori
bodyText: Mikadiyori is an izakaya serving authentic yakitori and omakase. Sit at the counter for a true Tokyo-like experience, complemented by a carefully curated sake selection throughout the evening.

title: Stadshuskällaren
bodyText: The only restaurant where guests can order any Nobel menu since 1901, served on official dinnerware in the banquet building. Jonas Bohlin's redesign pairs modern interiors with original 1920s décor.

title: Agnes
bodyText: Relaxed neighborhood bistro with a confident seasonal menu, curated wines, and warm service. Agnes blends Mediterranean and Asian flavors into comfort-driven dishes, a dependable favorite night after night.

title: Carbon
bodyText: Guided by precision and passion in the kitchen, Carbon delivers thoughtful, finely tuned cooking shaped by Jean Henkel, where technique, flavor, and a strong sense of identity come together.

title: Celeste
bodyText: Playful yet precise, Celeste offers a fine-dining experience where each dish is paired with a choice of wine, cocktail, or non-alcoholic match, showcasing creativity with confidence and clarity.

title: Coco & Carmen
bodyText: A playful fine-dining bistro with a creative tasting menu blending Nordic and global flavors, where dishes may range from scallop beignets to bright sea buckthorn sorbet. Perfect for a fun dinner.

title: DoMa | Matsalen
bodyText: What began as a living-room supper club in 2014 led Tea Malmegård and Viktor Lejon to open their restaurant in 2020, with two tasting menus showcasing ingredients grown by the couple on Ingarö.

title: Essence
bodyText: Stefan Taylor’s one-man fine dining experience offers front-row seats at the kitchen counter, where a multi-course tasting menu highlights premium local ingredients in an interactive setting.

title: Trattoria La Strega
bodyText: La Strega draws on northern Italian traditions from Piedmont, Lombardy, and Triveneto, serving honest, well-crafted dishes rooted in heritage, paired with a strong focus on biodynamic and natural wines.

title: At Six Dining Room
bodyText: Art by Jaume Plensa and Olafur Eliasson welcomes guests at the design-oriented Hotel At Six. In the restaurant, the Nordic-European menu is rivaled by a wine list with over 400 labels, all available by the glass.

title: Brasserie 1742
bodyText: Karim Khouani, who earned one of Malmö’s first stars, brought his expertise to the Kingdom of Crystal. At Kosta Boda Art Hotel, the tasting menu features exclusive ingredients like Wagyu, caviar, lobster, and scallops.

title: Flora
bodyText: Views across organically farmed vineyards to the sea make a visit to Thora Vingård’s restaurant extra sweet. Chef Tobias Millqvist creates seasonal dishes designed to pair with the estate’s Pinot Noir and Solaris.

title: Riche
bodyText: Inspired by Paris's Café Riche, this grand dining room became an icon after Tore Wretman's postwar revival. Today it boasts its own butcher, fishing boat, and a cellar of more than 900 wines.

title: Tage
bodyText: Perched on the 13th floor of KUST Hotell, this steakhouse offers panoramic views. A sky bar—the highest on the Norrland coast—sits one floor above. Under chef Håvard Santi, the menu focuses on grilled cuts.

title: Berns Asiatiska
bodyText: Sweden’s first Chinese restaurant opened here in 1944; today the kitchen ranges confidently across Thailand, Korea and Japan, all within the chandelier-lit grandeur of Berns Salonger, the city’s storied 1863 landmark.

title: Vita Amandi
bodyText: Set in a converted church where the altarpiece remains, this striking restaurant serves a tasting menu built around the evening's wines. Pairings are encouraged, with access to the cellar for further discoveries.

title: Animo
bodyText: A lively neo-bistro marked by genuine hospitality, confident cooking, expressive flavors, and seasonal produce, Animo balances modern technique with an easygoing, social atmosphere.

title: Bistro Zissou
bodyText: Family-run Bistro Zissou in Gamla Stan blends classic French cooking with a personal touch, as chef Kalle Lindborg and Emma Skerfe cultivate a warm, local atmosphere with a thoughtfully curated wine list.

title: Black Milk Gastro Bar
bodyText: At Black Milk Gastro Bar, omakase is reimagined through an ever-changing menu, blending Japanese tradition with global ingredients, bold flavors, and a lively yet intimate, modern setting.

title: Creo
bodyText: Reached by a staircase, this intimate upper-floor dining room feels like a private apartment. Modern fusion cooking is served in mid-sized dishes and as four- or seven-course tasting menus with drink pairings.

title: Lilla Bjers
bodyText: On a farm 7 km south of Visby, the Hoas family grows organic crops in open fields and tunnels, supplying a greenhouse restaurant and year-round farm shop. In the Gotland dialect, the name means “small mountain”.

title: Mýran
bodyText: Mýran feels more like a private supper club than a restaurant—warm, informal and social, where long dinners often drift into late-night conversations, shared bottles and an easy sense of harmony.

title: Triton
bodyText: Triton offers a flexible, produce-led menu shaped by what’s best at market, where vegetables, pasta, and lightly cured fish meet a relaxed Nordic bistro approach, with wine and vinyl setting the tone.

title: Banken Två Rum & Kök
bodyText: Housed in the janitor’s flat (“two rooms and a kitchen”) of a former bank, this fine dining room still feels like a private home. The host couple, Ingemar and Eva Eberstål, guide guests through multi-course menus.

title: Bar Agrikultur
bodyText: A relaxed yet thoughtful local bistro, Bar Agrikultur focuses on seasonal produce, vegetable-driven dishes, and carefully chosen wines and gin, delivering an honest dining experience.

title: Bruntegården
bodyText: Locals deliver foraged mushrooms, cloudberries and perch straight to the kitchen, where Magnus and Linn Ollas craft their distinctive “fäbod crossover” cuisine, blending rustic farmstead traditions with creative techniques.

title: Bryggargatan
bodyText: Icelandic chef Jón Óskar Arnason and sommelier Sarah from Piteå run this restaurant, where tasting menus showcase a vibrant mix of Arctic ingredients, underscoring Swedish Lapland's rise as a serious dining destination.

title: Flammans Skafferi
bodyText: The stone oven is the center of this exclusive mountain outpost with only 24 seats. Chef Lena Flaten develops “relationsmat”: food based on cooperation with growers, hunters, and fishermen in the area.

title: Forshems Gästgivaregård
bodyText: Open since 1564, this is Sweden’s oldest documented inn. Miriam and Stefan Johansson work with more than 100 local suppliers for their ambitious tasting menus and founded Kinnekulle Brewery in 2002.

title: Frö
bodyText: In 2017, three alumni of Oaxen Krog, Fäviken, and Gastrologik planted this culinary “seed” (frö) in a timber lodge near Hundfjället’s slopes. Most ingredients for the tasting menu come from Dalarna.

title: Hachi
bodyText: Eight counter seats face the chef at this intimate omakase bar. Guests can expect around 20 seasonal servings in the form of sushi and small plates, served piece by piece. Sake pairing available.

title: Hotell Borgholm
bodyText: On Öland, Christofer Johansson cooks seasonal dishes inspired by the island’s nature. Closed recently, it reopens in April with the same focus, now also à la carte. Points awarded pre-reopening.

title: Jord
bodyText: Reopened recently with a passion for Nordic flavors and sustainable, local gastronomy, now offering shorter menus. Recognized for its game focus, the kitchen has expanded to include fish and seafood.

title: Mutantur
bodyText: Mutantur is a celebrated Malmö food bar by chef-owner Alexander Sjögren, offering elegant, ever-changing small dishes with a strong seasonal and creative focus, paired with curated wine choices.

title: Ölme Prästgård Gästgiveri
bodyText: Set among oaks and maples in rural Värmland, this 1792 vicarage now serves as a guesthouse with an ambitious, Nordic-minded restaurant. Wine tastings, weekend packages, and festive buffets give reasons to return.

title: Västergatan
bodyText: Västergatan is a neighborhood favorite that balances warmth and ambition, offering flavor-driven cooking in an intimate setting where friendliness, value, and hospitality define the experience.

title: Villa Anna
bodyText: With backgrounds in acclaimed Swedish restaurants, chefs Rafael Löfstedt and Markus Arkevid now lead the kitchen at this boutique hotel. The menu showcases Nordic cuisine with local, often organic ingredients.

title: Washoku TOMO
bodyText: Washoku Tomo is an intimate counter restaurant led by chef-owner Tomoko Hayashi, serving pristine fish and seafood alongside home-style Japanese dishes, paired with a carefully curated sake selection.

title: TAK
bodyText: Frida Ronge has shaped this rooftop complex around a Nordic-Japanese approach. The main restaurant highlights raw preparations, while the izakaya upstairs serves small plates at shared high tables.

title: Amano
bodyText: Zander from Lake Hjälmaren, wild mushrooms from nearby forests, and oil from Julita form the foundation of the kitchen. Set menus and à la carte, plus one of Sweden’s widest selections of Italian wines.

title: Arctic Bath
bodyText: This floating hotel sits on the Lule River in Lapland. Chef David Staf combines Sámi traditions with Asian techniques in a five-course menu, served in a dining room with pine wood and Baltic Grey limestone.

title: Atmosfär
bodyText: The food concept centers on medium-sized plates designed for mixing and matching. A lunch dish of the day is offered Monday through Friday. Thanks to heaters, the glass-walled terrace is accessible year-round.

title: Bar Montan
bodyText: Concrete walls, white tablecloths, tiles, and dark brown chairs: This 2023 opening created a distinctive design in a converted slaughterhouse. The compact menu pairs refined seasonal plates with natural wine.

title: Bistron
bodyText: American chef Brian Landry brings global influences to this waterfront spot beside Norrbotten Theater, working with Nordic ingredients. Padded chairs, posters, and decorative lamps give the room a feminine touch.

title: Bord 27
bodyText: After restaurateur Peter Orrmyr opened this small neighborhood restaurant in 2015, it soon became a local favorite. The menu blends Swedish, French, Spanish, and Asian influences. A selection of natural wines.

title: Brygghuset
bodyText: Reine Patriksson opened this harbor restaurant in 1999; his whisky bar has some 3,200 bottles. Local fishermen supply lobster and shrimp; the herring lunch buffet makes the ferry ride from Lysekil worthwhile.

title: Chez Jolie
bodyText: At Chez Jolie, chef Mikael Einarsson leads a brasserie kitchen inspired by Paris and rural France, serving classics in an elegant, wood-panelled setting that feels like a calm retreat from the city.

title: DoMa | Bistro
bodyText: A modern neighborhood favorite by Viktor Lejon and Tea Malmegård, now offering both fine dining and a more relaxed bistro. Contemporary cooking is matched with warmth, hospitality and an easy, lively vibe.

title: Eriksberg | Havsörnen
bodyText: Game from Eriksberg’s own herds of deer, wild boar and European bison lies at the heart of the menu, refined with herbs from the on-site garden. Diners look out over the nature reserve where the animals roam freely.

title: Fotografiska
bodyText: Perched atop Fotografiska, this contemporary dining room presents its ever-evolving menu as The 5th Exhibition, with inventive dishes offered both à la carte and as an eight-course tasting.

title: Galleriet
bodyText: At lakeside Görvälns Slott, an adults-only boutique hotel, the restaurant focuses on Swedish seasonal ingredients. A French-leaning wine list features prestige Champagnes and Coravin pours by the glass.

title: Inez & Ernst
bodyText: Named after the owners' grandparents, this restaurant at Sankt Jörgen Park Resort continues time-honored traditions such as brining, salting, drying and pickling. The wine list features Solaris from the estate's own vineyard.

title: Jernbruket
bodyText: In a former ironworks, where heat once forged metal and now shapes the food, chefs cook over wood fire. Local meat and vegetables meet on the grill, while natural wines and craft beer fill the glasses.

title: Kattilakoski
bodyText: When architect Mats Winsa designed this restaurant, he added panoramic windows to frame the Kattilakoski rapids on the Torne River. Australian chef Taz Huggins cooks with local produce from the valley.

title: Nästgårds Gårdsrestaurang
bodyText: Evenings often begin with a stroll through the kitchen garden, where Johan Rudsby shows the ingredients behind the meal. The ten-course menu is built around organic produce from their own farm and selected suppliers.

title: Niesti
bodyText: Sámi food culture meets modern gastronomy at Copperhill Mountain Lodge's restaurant, 730 meters above sea level. The kitchen tells stories through each dish about where the ingredients were caught, grown, or picked.

title: ROT
bodyText: At Fabriken Furillen, chef Luqaz Ottosson and glass artist Jennie Olofsson serve a five-course menu with Gotland ingredients cooked in a wood-fired oven, plus occasional workshop dinners.

title: Simsons Restaurang & Deli
bodyText: Chef-sommelier Carl Bodin Svensk and partner Mika run this summer restaurant in a vicarage built in 1877. The kitchen turns organic ingredients into set menus, served in the garden or the historic dining room.

title: Sjömagasinet - Klippans Kulturreservat
bodyText: Set in a 1775 East India Company warehouse, this split-level seafood institution serves classic fish dishes upstairs with harbor views and a confidently curated wine list.

title: Stockholms Stadshotell | Bistro
bodyText: In an 1875 building honoring Oscar I of Sweden, this bistro keeps its charcoal grill glowing. Head chef Olle T. Cellton cooks Southern European classics and thoughtfully composed daily lunches with care.

title: Teatergrillen
bodyText: Teatergrillen is a heritage Stockholm institution serving traditional Swedish dishes with French influence, prepared with precision and a contemporary touch, alongside an elegant wine bar.

title: Trädgårdsgatan 26
bodyText: Siblings Jonas and Sara Åhman run a 16-seat room in one of the town’s oldest houses. A weekly set menu highlights modern Swedish cooking with Öland produce, matched with a curated wine pairing.

title: Vin O Deli Karlstad
bodyText: Mediterranean-inspired tapas, seven-course menus, and a broad wine list draw locals back to this central bistro. Wine experts lead regular tastings, pairing quality bottles with local cheeses and charcuterie.

title: Bjertorp Slott Restaurang
bodyText: Sweden’s youngest Art Nouveau castle, designed by Ferdinand Boberg in 1914, now hosts chef Christopher Lai. His eight-course tasting menu refines seasonal produce and local favorites from the Varaslätten plain.

title: Brasserie Astoria
bodyText: A classic international brasserie led by the widely acclaimed Björn Frantzén, Astoria blends effortless chic with all-day dining, city energy, and exceptionally attentive, polished service.

title: Bungenäs Kalklada & Matsal
bodyText: Each summer, the Aristo team from Stockholm cooks on Gotland’s car-free Bungenäs peninsula in a former limestone quarry. Kalkladan serves casual lunches, while Matsalen focuses on dinner.

title: Champagnebaren
bodyText: A natural destination for Champagne lovers, Champagnebaren pours everything from elegant classics to rare bottles, paired with carefully crafted fish and vegetarian dishes rooted in local produce.

title: Farang
bodyText: A vibrant Southeast Asian restaurant with an open kitchen and a share-food philosophy. Bold Thai, Vietnamese, and Malaysian flavors, plus what many call the city's best soft-shell crab.

title: Fjällnäs Est. 1882
bodyText: Sweden’s oldest (and first) mountain hotel overlooks Lake Malmagen near the Norwegian border. Refined tasting menus translate wild herbs and regionally hunted game into contemporary Nordic fine dining.

title: Konstnärsbaren
bodyText: Open since 1931, the “artist’s bar” keeps Björn Hedvall’s original interiors and the wall paintings by Isaac Grünewald. Swedish husmanskost and a serious wine cellar remain central to its enduring appeal.

title: Mancini
bodyText: Run by Claudio Mancini since 1988, with sommelier Giancarlo Clark presiding over a 2,000-bottle cellar, the kitchen champions hand-stretched pasta, pristine seafood and white truffles when in season.

title: Prinsen
bodyText: This elegant brasserie has welcomed generations of artists, writers, and business figures. Under head chef Karl Mogren, the kitchen cooks from scratch, blending French technique with a distinctly Swedish character.

title: Sperling & Co
bodyText: After winning Chef of the Year in 2024, Michael Andersson opened this grill restaurant. Designed by Dinell Johansson, the two-floor space features dark ash wood, brass and a lantern skylight.

title: Brasserie Draken
bodyText: On the 33rd floor of the Clarion Hotel Draken, this brasserie overlooks the river and harbor. Sommelier Andreas Hiller curates over 800 labels, while the kitchen serves brasserie classics.

title: Dorsia
bodyText: An elegant dining room inside a five-star boutique hotel, infused with La Belle Époque glamor. Known for indulgent Saturday long lunches, as well as refined à la carte dining and classic afternoon tea.

title: Vingården
bodyText: Daniel Crespi's barbecue restaurant opens each summer in a charming Old Town courtyard. The wine program is vast, with up to 100 options by the glass and a cellar list of 3,000 labels. Open May through August only.

title: Matildas
bodyText: A beloved neighborhood restaurant run by chefs and owners Frida and Johan Flodman. With a focus on sustainability, the seasonal menu highlights carefully sourced ingredients and sincere cooking.

title: RiRi
bodyText: At Riri, the open kitchen puts the charcoal grill center stage, where fish, meat, and seasonal vegetables are cooked over fire, finished with sauces and fresh accents, alongside a thoughtfully curated natural wine list.

title: Amalia
bodyText: Led by Anton Lindqvist, Amalia champions fine produce, inventive flavor combinations and a warm neo-bistro sensibility that sets it apart in Stockholm's contemporary dining scene.

title: Ärla
bodyText: Ärla is a small neighborhood bistro by Lotta Karlsson and Patric Blomquist, offering seasonal, locally driven Nordic fine dining cooking throughout at an approachable price point.

title: Bang Matbar
bodyText: Guest chefs and pop-ups bring variety to this ambitious spot throughout the year. The “food bar” is located in the 1925 Amerikahuset, once home to an intercontinental shipping line. Wednesday to Saturday only.

title: Dagmar
bodyText: Next door to Östermalms Saluhall, this restaurant forms part of the boutique Hotel Villa Dagmar. Mediterranean influences shape the menu, while in the glass-roofed atrium, the Garden Bar keeps the evening flowing.

title: Klostergatan 5
bodyText: Opened in 2019, this bistro run by the Triller family starts off its menu with Swedish farmhouse cheeses, followed by a concise selection of starters and mains. The dynamic wine list is updated continually.

title: Nook
bodyText: Led by sommelier Alexander Bäckman and chef Gustaf Larsson, this restaurant blends Nordic ingredients with Asian flavors. Now in its third location, it serves set menus uniting both traditions.

title: Norra Hamnen 5
bodyText: Overlooking the West Sea, this harbor restaurant highlights langoustines, oysters and mussels from the coast. The kitchen created two gins with Nyfjäll Destilleri, and terraces maximise the views.

title: Poppy
bodyText: Poppy offers a seasonal Nordic menu with a clear focus on Swedish ingredients, served in an intimate, characterful setting where the open kitchen brings warmth and energy to the experience.

title: Project
bodyText: Created by Anna and Cameron Irving, Project has grown from a modest café into a highly regarded destination, offering refined cooking in a warm, intimate setting that feels personal and assured.

title: Skärets Krog & Café
bodyText: With Thomas Sjögren, Chef of the Year 2015, the kitchen turns local seafood into three- and five-course menus. The prawn sandwich (räkmacka) was invented here in 1931. Finish with drinks at the Piano Bar.

title: Svartsö Krog
bodyText: Chef shapes this vegetable-forward restaurant, accessible only by boat. The terrace on the bay rewards visitors with rosé and tarte flambée on summer evenings. Glamping accommodation is available.

title: Vesterbrunn Brasserie & Bar
bodyText: Named for a historic spring on Lake Munksjön, this brasserie is led by head chef Anne, who works exclusively with Swedish ingredients. Sommelier David pairs her tasting menus with biodynamic wines and local soft drinks.

title: Aleks y Filip
bodyText: Galician octopus and 35-day dry-aged beef are on the menu at this family-run Spanish restaurant. Head chef Andres works the open kitchen, while brothers Aleks and Filip oversee a wine list with 200 labels.

title: Bulot
bodyText: Tucked inside Göteborgs Saluhall, Bar Bulot is a refined spot much loved for lunch, serving carefully crafted small and medium-sized dishes, best enjoyed with a thoughtfully chosen glass of wine.

title: Dryck & Mat
bodyText: Wine leads the way at this fine dining venue in a former train station: The kitchen crafts its set menu around specific bottles, listing the wine first and the dish second for each of the four courses.

title: Imilla
bodyText: Two chefs run both kitchen and floor in this restaurant with some 20 seats. A “chef’s choice” tasting menu blends Nordic touches with French inspiration in six courses. A personal dining experience since 2020.

title: Kittelfjäll Värdshus
bodyText: After 18 seasons in Åre, chef Jasper Bergström opened this restaurant with his wife Lotta, the sommelier. The kitchen uses local game and fish, alongside vegetables grown on site.

title: Kockeriet
bodyText: Established in 2014, Kockeriet is a cherished Malmö dining room built on ingredient-driven cooking, where seasonality and sustainability quietly guide the menu with a clear sense of quality.

title: Köksbaren
bodyText: Head sommelier Kristian Rönnlund oversees a cellar of around 500 wines at this gastropub with an informal atmosphere. The kitchen works with ingredients from Västerbotten, grilling dry-aged meat in a charcoal oven.

title: La Ruelle
bodyText: The name translates to “the alley,” and the location matches: a tiny bistro tucked into a narrow lane in central Uppsala. Owners Gustav Petrusson and Erik Millroth bring experience from Frantzén to a rustic French menu.

title: Lilla Ego
bodyText: Lilla Ego is a much-loved Stockholm dining room led by Tom Sjöstedt and Daniel Räms, offering expressive, contemporary cuisine rooted in Swedish flavors, with a strong personal touch.

title: Minh Mat
bodyText: Spices from minority villages in northwestern Vietnam, especially Thái, Mường, and H’mông traditions, define this bistro. Owner Minh Du Alneng pairs authentic flavors with local Swedish produce.

title: Natur
bodyText: A short, produce-driven menu meets a wine list known for its natural options. The warm dining room features artworks on the walls, while on the summer terrace the city backdrop does the decorating.

title: Nektar mat & vin
bodyText: Opened by Eric Seger and Embla Brorsson after stints in leading kitchens across Stockholm and Copenhagen, this intimate bistro champions wine-led dining, favoring clean, precise natural styles over the experimental.

title: Nergården
bodyText: Lake Sillen sets the scene at this adults-only boutique hotel. Chef Johan Ahlvik designs menus around ingredients from farms in Sörmland, pairing the food with organic and biodynamic wines.

title: NOI Stockholm
bodyText: Wingårdhs Architects designed this subterranean restaurant at Nobis Hotel, where olive-green leather banquettes line walnut-paneled walls. Stefano Catenacci advises a modern European menu.

title: Peterson's Krog
bodyText: The car-free island of Käringön, reached by ferry from Orust, is home to this seafood-focused summer institution. Autumn brings lobster feasts before the season closes; Christmas buffet with delicacies from the sea.

title: Postgatan
bodyText: Chef Viktor Hallberg previously worked at PM & Vänner before co-opening Postgatan on the namesake street in 2015. The fine bistro serves modern cuisine and has a wine list focused on classic European regions.

title: Prästgatan
bodyText: Taken over by the Spiseriet team in 2023, this bistro pairs an ambitious wine program with informal cooking. On weekdays, the lunch offers hearty dishes of the day or a three-course menu for those with time.

title: Rå
bodyText: Hearty dishes make this modern steakhouse a local favorite, where grill platters are served on Wednesdays and Thursdays. On the ambitious cocktail list, the creamy princess cake drink is a signature.

title: Salt & Sill
bodyText: Sweden’s first floating hotel is paired with a renowned seafood restaurant. The house classic is called sillplankan: a “herring board” with fillets in eight homemade marinades. Bohuslän archipelago views.

title: Sillen & Makrillen
bodyText: Dining in a glass pavilion by the water comes with sweeping views towards Denmark. The menu centers on local fish and shellfish, from toast Skagen and grilled lobster to the house herring and mackerel.

title: Skrea Matbruk
bodyText: Local produce meets Italian technique in hand-rolled pasta and small plates. Founded by TV chef Lisa Lemke, the restaurant overlooks vineyards, with a nearby distillery supplying gin for its cocktails.

title: Spiseriet
bodyText: Peter Halldén opened this farmhouse restaurant with childhood friend Linus Boman in 2019. The converted bull stable sits within Johnssons Gård, where a bakery, brewery, and cheese counter share the courtyard.

title: Sturehof
bodyText: Sturehof is a long-standing Stockholm institution, known for classic brasserie cooking rooted in Swedish tradition with French influence, served in a lively, elegant setting, open seven days a week.

title: Voisine
bodyText: This French-inspired bistro was opened by sommeliers Béatrice Becher and Jonas Sandberg. Seasonal plates are joined by classic desserts, while a strong wine list draws on their acclaimed neighboring bar, Folii.

title: Asian post office
bodyText: Opened in 2018 by the Family of Supper collective, this pan-Asian dining bar takes guests on a flavor-led journey from Beirut to Tokyo, with sharing plates backed by a cellar of more than 400 wines.

title: Barón
bodyText: In a former bank with high ceilings, owner Aram Gomah serves Spanish-inspired tapas with a Swedish accent. Sharing plates (octopus is a highlight!) and well-made cocktails suit the elegant space.

title: Bistro Le Garage
bodyText: Seasonal cooking unfolds inside the Umedalen Sculpture Park, home to works by Louise Bourgeois, Anish Kapoor, and Antony Gormley. The kitchen keeps things Swedish, while the wine list looks abroad.

title: Bistron Torekov
bodyText: Torekov Hotell’s dining room overlooks the terrace and pool. Local meat from Lindegrens, chicken from Bjärefågel, Båstad honey, and Torekov asparagus appear on a menu that changes with the seasons.

title: Brasserie Godot
bodyText: Since 2001, founders Mattias Rosenbaum and Staffan Svederman have remained hands-on, often greeting guests themselves. The kitchen honors French traditions, while modern and classic cocktails round off the evening.

title: Camp Ripan
bodyText: Three cultures shape this restaurant in the country’s northernmost city: Swedish, Sámi, and Torne Valley Finnish. Reindeer, Arctic char, and cloudberries lead the menu. On lucky nights, the Northern Lights appear.

title: Copine by Jim&Jacob
bodyText: Named for the French word for “girlfriend,” this Mediterranean restaurant from the Jim & Jacob team has counter seating and a dining room overlooking the kitchen. Wine by the glass, bottle, or half bottle.

title: Freyja + Söder
bodyText: Seasonal Nordic cooking with a modern edge on Södermalm in Stockholm. A chef-driven spot by Emma Shields, where thoughtful flavors, natural wines, and a lively atmosphere come together.

title: Gimo Herrgård Restaurang
bodyText: Sweden’s first Gustavian manor from the 1760s houses a restaurant that cooks with local ingredients from Roslagen and nearby farms. Refined dining under chandeliers, plus a private wine cellar for tastings.

title: Johans Krog
bodyText: Owner Johan Gustafsson runs this French-inspired bistro in a traditional wooden house on Marstrand Island. The rotisserie features on the menu, while a long wine list rewards curious drinkers.

title: Klostergatans Vin & Delikatess
bodyText: Inspired by brasseries, the kitchen blends French classics with seasonal Swedish flavors. The 16-page wine list leans towards Old World selections, offering breadth alongside an impressive range by the glass.

title: Le Bon Canon
bodyText: Wine guides the experience at this bistro, where Marcus Maijanen curates a list with a strong French presence. Southern European bistro cooking with Nordic restraint delivers dishes that pair naturally with the drinks.

title: Maritime
bodyText: Perched above the harbor with views over the Öresund, this dining room belongs to Grand Hôtel Mölle, run by the Dahlberg family since 1963. Seasonal menus feature vegetables from their greenhouse in Brunnby.

title: Skoogs Krog
bodyText: Erik and his team cook tasting menus from what the mountains provide. House-pressed berry and flower juices provide a well-matched non-alcoholic pairing. Hotel rooms include access to a hot tub and sauna.

title: Talldungens Gårdshotell
bodyText: Talldungen is an intimate countryside retreat where heartfelt hospitality and a deep connection to the land shape both the stay and the food, rooted in flavor, warmth, and authenticity.

title: Värdshuset Lindgården
bodyText: Walnut and mulberry trees shade this inn’s terrace, lending a Mediterranean feel. The kitchen works with Gotland producers, offers autumn truffle menus, and pairs dishes with European wines and 50 gins.

title: Wagners Bistro
bodyText: Wagners Bistro is led by chef-owner Ulf Wagner, where comforting flavors meet refined technique, drawing on Nordic and French traditions and supported by a notably strong wine list.

title: Bonnie's
bodyText: Playfully named after Bonnie Parker, this restaurant fills the hall of the 1910 building now home to Bank Hotel. Blue-green stucco columns and a six-meter glass ceiling frame international dishes.

title: Operabaren
bodyText: In Stockholm's historic opera house, Operabaren is a long-standing institution serving traditional Swedish cooking. Classic interiors frame warm, skillful hospitality and a reassuring sense of continuity.

title: Tjoget
bodyText: Four concepts under one roof—dining room, wine bar, beer café and a cocktail bar often ranked among the world's best. Sharing plates bring Mediterranean flavors together with North African and Middle Eastern notes.

title: Rådhustorget No:1A
bodyText: Icelandic chef Knútur Kristjánsson took over this gastrobar in 2021 and brought his fine-dining experience to a casual setting. The dishes, composed of three to four components, showcase local vegetables and meats.

title: Gastro Gaspari
bodyText: A destination restaurant in the Skåne countryside, where seasonal local ingredients shape a focused tasting menu. Refined cooking meets a calm, rural setting at historic Flyinge Kungsgård.

title: Brasserie Fjällköket
bodyText: Part of Abisko Mountain Lodge, this Slow Food member sources moose, Arctic char, and cloudberries from the surrounding wilderness and waters. The “coast to coast” tasting menu consists of six seasonal courses.

title: Brunnsgatan 41
bodyText: Exposed brick walls and a lofty dining room create a living room feel at this contemporary dining bar. Creative plates like Sichuan-baked cabbage and jalapeño-topped scallops encourage mixing and sharing.

title: Daawat Masthugget
bodyText: In 1971, Surjit Singh Ahluwalia opened one of Sweden’s first Indian restaurants, introducing new spices and dishes. Decades later, his sons continue the legacy in Masthugget and at two other locations.

title: Gaijin
bodyText: This sushi bar takes its name from the Japanese word for “outsider” and views Nippon cooking through a playful lens. Opened in 2025, it goes beyond nigiri and sashimi with small, creative dishes.

title: Han i Hörnet
bodyText: Elin and Mattias Holmberg opened this 28-seat bistro with wine bar, earning a reputation for craftsmanship. A concise menu highlights local beef and seasonal vegetables, with beer sourced from Åkers Styckebruk.

title: Hantverket
bodyText: Hantverket is a warm, lively dining room where chef-patron Stefan Ekengren reimagines Swedish home-style classics with creativity and precision, bringing a distinctly modern touch to dishes rooted in tradition.

title: House Of Ven
bodyText: The island of Ven has only about 400 inhabitants, and over 30 local companies supply this guesthouse, including Spirit of Hven, which produces whisky and gin. Its kitchen serves a seasonal menu inspired by the four seasons.

title: Hunger och Törst
bodyText: Overlooking the Umeälven River, this central destination serves tasting menus that evolve weekly. Guests may choose three, five or seven courses, with drink pairings composed by the in-house sommeliers.

title: Johan P
bodyText: Founded in 1981, this classic fish restaurant takes its name from Johan Persson, later shortened. Chequered floors and a seafood counter set the scene for the day’s catch, completed by oysters and champagne.

title: Kaifo
bodyText: The Orrmyr family added Kaifo to their Gothenburg portfolio. The name signals a “happy Asian fusion” approach, expressed in dishes like steambuns and sashimi.

title: Las Brasas
bodyText: This grill-driven tapas bar takes its name from the Spanish for “the embers.” Alongside smaller plates with fish, vegetables, and croquettes, the meaty mains feature Wagyu beef, pluma ibérico, and Swedish entrecote.

title: Matbaren Borgholm
bodyText: At this modern bistro in Societetsparken, guests order mid-sized plates in any sequence. European influences meet high-quality ingredients, with staff on hand to recommend drinks to complement each course.

title: Misshumasshu
bodyText: The duo behind Adam/Albin enriches Sweden’s oldest shopping arcade with rust-red dining spaces. Positioned as an izakaya-brasserie-bar mashup, it serves starters, mains, and an omakase sharing menu.

title: Nana Omakase
bodyText: An intimate seven-seat counter in central Stockholm, Nana Omakase blends Japanese omakase craft with Nordic seasonal produce, shaping a tasting menu defined by precision and quietly luxurious ingredients.

title: Rolfs Hav
bodyText: Rolfs Hav centers on pristine fish and shellfish, handled with restraint to let natural flavors shine. Created by Johan Jureskog and Klas Ljungquist, it offers seafood in an unpretentious setting.

title: Stångs Magasin
bodyText: Chef Jonas Alvin runs a KRAV-certified restaurant in an 1805 warehouse, sourcing from regional farms and small-scale producers. Swedish classics are reinterpreted with game, rainbow trout, and foraged ingredients.

title: Surfers
bodyText: Known for its playful, uncompromising take on regional Chinese cooking, Surfers offers an energetic, vibrant dining experience, where sharing dishes and baijiu tastings shape the evening.

title: Tripletta
bodyText: For Robert Rudinski, opening his third restaurant at this address felt like coming home. Named after the Italian word for a hat trick, it serves modern Italian cooking with a strong sense of regional variety.

title: Tumült
bodyText: Chef Daniel Müllern returned to his native Ystad with this relaxed neighborhood spot. Scandinavian, Mediterranean, and Asian flavors meet in sharing plates of varying sizes, with schnitzel a steady favorite.

title: Acaza
bodyText: In 2023, Acaza gave Stockholm a proper Portuguese “taberna”. The bright, colorful room feels like Lisbon, and the staff speak the language. The wine list spans native grapes from Douro to Alentejo.

title: Årstiderna i Kockska Huset
bodyText: This vaulted brick cellar dates back to the 1500s, when Malmö’s mayor Jörgen Kock built his mansion on the site. Since 1967, the restaurant has paired Swedish and European classics with produce from Skåne.

title: Aster
bodyText: Centered on a grand wood-fired oven, Aster is a refined dining destination celebrated for its expertly crafted dishes and warm, unpretentious atmosphere, earning its place among Malmö's most admired restaurants.

title: Båthuset Krog & Bar
bodyText: The floating restaurant boasts views across Lake Mälaren and a nautical interior. Since taking over in 2017, the three chefs have sharpened the focus on seasonal Nordic produce, particularly seafood.

title: Bistro Grodlår & Timjan
bodyText: Henrik Daleskog and Louise Sevedsson run this bistro, “Frog Leg and Thyme,” where the Bjäre Peninsula meets Burgundy. The menu features whole chicken from Munka-Ljungby, escargots, and a wine list with a clear French focus.

title: Björk Topprestaurang & Fjällbar
bodyText: At the top of the Solkatt lift, this award-winning restaurant is known for its distinctive architecture. A five-course tasting menu is built around ingredients sourced from Swedish Lapland.

title: Bloom in the Park
bodyText: Neither menu nor wine list is revealed until guests receive a QR code at departure, giving the kitchen full seasonal freedom. The dining room overlooks the lake at Pildammsparken.

title: Bomans Restaurang
bodyText: The Boman family has run inns for generations, and today’s kitchen serves Swedish classics with local and often organic ingredients. Behind the traditional red façade, the eclectic safari-style interior is a surprise.

title: Boqueria
bodyText: Boqueria channels Spanish food culture through small plates, bold flavors and a spirited, sociable atmosphere, equally suited to quick bites or long, wine-fuelled evenings in good company.

title: Brasserie Tullhuset
bodyText: Set in a former 1800s customs house, this international brasserie serves Nordic sushi and dishes built on local ingredients. A terrace overlooking the Motala River completes the setting.

title: Brezza
bodyText: Brezza, Italian for “breeze,” combines restaurant and enoteca, with a cellar stocked with icons like Sassicaia, Masseto, and Tignanello. The kitchen produces house-made pasta, wood-fired pizza, and prepared charcuterie.

title: Bryggcafét
bodyText: Set on the jetty by the harbor, this family-run restaurant overlooks the boats passing on Bottnefjorden. Fish and seafood dominate the menu, while the wine list focuses on France and the United States.

title: Bryggerikrogen Nora
bodyText: After years in Åre and Stockholm, Veronica Carlsson returned to her native Bergslagen region in 2015. In a former brewery, she pairs seasonal Swedish cooking with natural wines and local craft beers.

title: Bryggvingen
bodyText: On the island of Lyr, reached by ferry or private boat, the menu follows the daily catch of owner-fisherman Erik Lyräng. Dishes are served on a sea-view terrace, and an on-site fish shop offers takeaway.

title: Domtrappkällaren
bodyText: Housed in a 13th-century building beside Uppsala Cathedral, this long-standing restaurant serves Swedish classics. Sommeliers oversee an extensive wine list that complements the kitchen.

title: Elise
bodyText: Near the beach in Djupvik, chef Alex serves sharing plates built on island ingredients, paired with drinks from Kackelbryggeriet. Open only in summer, when locals and visitors gather for the long evening sun.

title: Epoque
bodyText: White tiles, artworks, and single shelves with wine bottles frame this neighborhood favorite near Götaplatsen. A charcoal grill, along with Swedish flavors and traditions, defines the seasonal menu.

title: Fjällkällans Kök
bodyText: In a mountain village of 49 vacation homes, this bistro prepares forest and lake ingredients in a Nordic style. Guests dine by the fire, surrounded by paintings and ceramics by regional artists.

title: Gåsemora Gårdskrog
bodyText: On Ingmar Bergman’s filming island Fårö, this restaurant uses historic farm buildings overlooking heathland and sea. The kitchen highlights local produce, such as Gotland lamb. Maria Blomdahl took over in 2025.

title: Grand Tenan
bodyText: Reached by ferry, this 1892 hotel has long drawn shellfish lovers. Chef Alexander Stärnerz works with Bohuslän lobster, langoustine and oysters, while sommelier Anders Pålsson oversees the cellar.

title: Gurras
bodyText: Chef Gustav Trägårdh's playful kitchen turns global street food into comforting, well-crafted dishes. Worldly flavors, inventive ideas and an easygoing atmosphere define the experience.

title: Harlequin
bodyText: An award-winning sommelier team steers the wine program at this northern Swedish restaurant. The kitchen uses produce from Västerbotten, changing the menu monthly to reflect what’s in season.

title: Jarlen
bodyText: Wine takes center stage at this French-style bistro, where the selection contains top producers worldwide. The kitchen follows suit with dishes like foie gras and moules crème. Regular winemaker dinners.

title: Jay Fu's
bodyText: Perched above the market hall with river views, this steakhouse blends American barbecue traditions with Asian flavors. Cocktails nod to 1960s hits, and the wine list features Californians such as Bond and Harlan.

title: La Cucina Italiana
bodyText: Founded by Pietro Fioriniello of Campania and now run by his son Alessio, this intimate trattoria seats six tables and serves compact tasting menus with a thoughtfully curated selection of Italian wines.

title: Le Petit Bistrot
bodyText: Petit Bistro is a welcoming, family-run neighborhood restaurant offering from-scratch French classics in a warm, bustling setting suited to both quiet dinners and relaxed get-togethers.

title: Linnéa&Peter
bodyText: A warm, welcoming neighborhood restaurant serving honest, carefully prepared dishes with respect for ingredients, paired with a thoughtful wine list—a place where everyone feels at home.

title: Marie Antoinette
bodyText: Distinct concepts keep this modern spot buzzing all week: sharing menus, an affordable Triple Treat with wine pairings on Tuesdays, and Oyster Happy Hour on Thursdays draw a steady after-work crowd.

title: Nya Hattfabriken
bodyText: Swedish classics meet French bistro cooking at this former hat shop, open since 2011. Toast Skagen, Wallenbergare, and meatballs share the menu with Moules Frites and a weekly slow-cooked special.

title: Omaka
bodyText: Fourth-generation brewer Hedda Spendrup opened this gastropub in the former School of Architecture in 2020. Chef Christian Siberg creates dishes to complement beers brewed on-site.

title: Portal
bodyText: Led by Klas Lindberg, Portal centers on high-quality local produce and Nordic flavors, drawing a lively crowd from lunch through to late evening for wine, craft beer and relaxed, all-day dining.

title: Pråmen
bodyText: Moored in Västerås harbor on Lake Mälaren, this elegant barge restaurant is truly unique. The focus is on one- or two-course lunches, with occasional seven-course tasting menus offered in the evening.

title: Publik Mat & Bar
bodyText: Jens and Andreas started with a fish cart in 2014 before opening this harbor-front bistro the following year. The kitchen blends West Coast seafood with Japanese and South American influences in its dishes.

title: Pumphuset Borstahusen
bodyText: Built in 1900 as part of a sugar works, this brick pump house at the harbor is now integrated into a cultural hub with a restaurant, art hall, and a small local museum. There are views over Öresund toward the island of Ven.

title: Rolfs Kök
bodyText: A long-standing Stockholm institution, Rolfs Kök is prized for unfussy cooking, anchored by slow-braised ox cheek, a house signature served in a buzzy room with effortless all-day appeal.

title: Sand
bodyText: Originally a grain warehouse from 1877, Hotel Skansen’s restaurant overlooks the sea. The kitchen sources from farms on the Bjäre Peninsula, and the wine list features more than a hundred labels.

title: Sardin
bodyText: Chefs Ola Wallberg and Simon Idmyr run this neighborhood spot with wine importer Kristin Idmyr. Spanish and Italian flavors define the menu, from nduja croquettes to steak tartare.

title: Sibbjäns
bodyText: This family-run farmstay offers farm-to-fork dining rooted in its own fields and gardens. Expect vegetable-oriented dishes shaped by the seasons, natural wines, and an immersive setting of alvar, forest, and nearby coastline.

title: Sofiero Slottsrestaurang
bodyText: Meals are served in a former royal summer palace completed in 1865. Seasonal Nordic cooking comes with views over Öresund and a famed rhododendron garden. A separate bistro sits in the old orangery.

title: Stufvenäs Gästgifveri
bodyText: Set by the coast near the Örarevet nature reserve, this Småland inn cooks Swedish dishes with a modern twist, using producers in Södermöre and the wider region. The wine cellar was rebuilt after a burglary in 2007.

title: Tavolo
bodyText: This Italian-American restaurant opened in 2020 inside a converted artillery stable, echoed by a replica of Leonardo’s horse sculpture over the bar. An open kitchen serves Neapolitan pizza and sharing plates.

title: Toso
bodyText: A five-meter reclining Buddha watches over the open kitchen at this Pan-Asian restaurant, opened in 2014. The menu draws flavors from across Asia, with many dishes designed for sharing.

title: Tranan
bodyText: Open since 1929, this institution blends Swedish comfort food with French bistro tradition. Fried herring with mashed potatoes has featured on the menu since the early days, while the cellar holds some 12,000 bottles.

title: Ulla Winbladh
bodyText: Built as a steam bakery for the 1897 World Fair, this villa now houses a beloved traditional restaurant. Named for Bellman's muse, it serves classic Swedish husmanskost with a clear sense of heritage.

title: Villa Strandvägen
bodyText: Housed in a historic villa from the late 19th century, Villa Strandvägen offers an intimate setting where dishes are cooked à la minute, creating a close connection between kitchen, craft, and guest.

title: Lammet & Grisen
bodyText: After Jan Richert brought the roast pig concept from Mallorca, this summer institution opened in 1969. Whole lamb and pork are turned on spits and carved in front of guests. On-site vineyard since 2025.

title: Spesso
bodyText: Set high above the city, Spesso offers a contemporary take on Italian cooking, where classic flavors meet modern expression, served in a stylish, welcoming setting suited to social dining.

title: Heaven 23
bodyText: Open since 2002 on the 23rd floor of Gothia Towers, this sky bar surveys the city from every angle. European dishes pair with mainly Austrian wines, including their own Blaufränkisch-based “23 Reasons”.

title: Allegrine
bodyText: A recent reset brings a new food bar, vibrant French small plates, generous shareable mains, and a broader wine-by-the-glass list. Restaurateur Danyel Couet shapes a relaxed yet confident experience.

title: Riket
bodyText: Two former Tempo chefs run this neighborhood spot by Davidshall Square, centering around a short seasonal menu and a wine list with a natural, craft-driven focus. The casual atmosphere makes it a favorite with regulars.

title: Smörtaxen
bodyText: Two creatives and a chef turned a former garage beside the citadel into what they call fun dining. In winter, a fixed, playful menu meets loud music; in summer, the concept shifts to drop-in service.

title: Bergmans Fisk Saltharsfjärden
bodyText: Seven generations of the Bergman family have fished these Baltic waters. Three cousins now run a complex with a smokery, shop, and restaurant. The salmon plank combines different preparation techniques on one plate.

title: Blue light Yokohama
bodyText: Shoes come off before settling into sunken horigotatsu tables at this Japanese izakaya. For over a decade, it has honored seasonal ingredients with quiet reverence and tradition; Sundays are devoted to ramen.

title: Brasserie Bobonne
bodyText: This intimate brasserie channels Parisian neighborhood charm, pairing classic French cooking with great wines and warm hospitality—ideal for lunch, dinner, or a quick stop at the adjoining wine bar.

title: Brasserie Park
bodyText: Småland flavors meet French traditions at this white-tablecloth brasserie. The popular seafood platter comes with tastes of lobster, crab, mussels, oysters, and shrimps. Around 15 culinary events per year.

title: Cuculo
bodyText: Named after the Italian word for cuckoo, this restaurant serves playful Mediterranean dishes with Swedish touches. A lively cocktail bar complements the menu with spritzes, Negroni twists and aperitivo-style drinks.

title: Dahlboms Mat & Bar
bodyText: Jonas Dahlbom, who won “Chef of the Year” in 1996, and his partner Pia opened this neighborhood spot in 2021. The menu is organized into four categories (greens, fish, meat, and sweets), with four options each.

title: Fabel
bodyText: This corner spot at Vasaplatsen has been a meeting place for Gothenburgers for over a century and was relaunched in 2024. Swedish-French classics are served in a room with green walls and classic wooden furniture.

title: Gotthards Krog
bodyText: In Umeå’s culinary quarter, Gotthards serves modern cuisine inspired by northern Sweden. Local produce, close ties to nearby artisans, and a strong sustainability focus shape the menu.

title: Hemmagastronomi
bodyText: Chef Simon Laiti returned to his hometown in 2008 to open his own place by the harbor. A restaurant, deli, and bakery share one roof, united by a focus on Norrbotten ingredients: game, vendace roe, and foraged berries.

title: Hillenberg
bodyText: A stylish, contemporary dining room where Southern European flavors meet Scandinavian restraint, creating a relaxed yet polished atmosphere under the guidance of Niklas Ekstedt, from lunch well into the night.

title: Izakaya Moshi
bodyText: Sandra and Daniel founded their gastropub in 2012 after an inspirational trip through Japan. Small plates and sushi cite broader Asian influences, with a sharing menu for two. The atmosphere is communal.

title: Lörudden
bodyText: In a historic fishing village, local boats and coastal waters supply the kitchen where Kenneth Sillman (aptly named) refines the catch of the day. Perch and whitefish from the Bothnian Sea are smoked on site.

title: Lux Dag för Dag
bodyText: Lux Dag för Dag is an ingredient-driven restaurant working closely with local farmers, serving seasonal cuisine that balances hearty comfort with quiet refinement in a beautiful setting.

title: NISCH
bodyText: Led by Claes Björling, Nisch offers a seasonal tasting menu built on precision and purity, with a quiet sense of focus running through the experience, alongside wines rooted in organic and biodynamic traditions.

title: R Asia
bodyText: Hidden behind an unassuming shopping center façade, R Asia focuses on regional Chinese cooking, with Hunan and Sichuan flavors at the core, rooted in classic Chinese banquet traditions.

title: A.Ts Krog
bodyText: The schnitzel is the dish that made André Edlund's neighborhood spot a local favorite. After winning Olympic gold with Sweden's junior culinary team, he returned north to cook in a distinctly European style.

title: Algot
bodyText: For chef Fredrik Craas and partner Milly, the food is defined by producers from the region: Beef comes from Naturgården, cheese from Kungsbacka and Almnäs. Even juices, wine, and spirits are Swedish.

title: ANTONIO'S
bodyText: Certified Neapolitan pizzaiolos and house-made pasta make this waterfront restaurant authentically Italian. The pizza Skagen stands out as a Nordic creation. Sunday brunch brings a surprise menu.

title: Åstols Rökeri
bodyText: On the car-free island of Åstol, this fish restaurant has welcomed guests since 1984. It smokes shrimp, salmon, and mackerel over alder chips next door. Ferry access from Rönnäng; open April to September.

title: Babette
bodyText: A restaurant with a strong focus on quality ingredients, Babette is known for its sourdough pizza alongside seasonal dishes, all served in a casual, buzzing atmosphere that draws a loyal local crowd.

title: Bouchon
bodyText: Bouchon captures the warmth of French bistro dining, with a clear nod to Lyon—rustic, expertly executed dishes served with charm, tradition, and a sense of ease.

title: Brasserie Maison
bodyText: This cozy, family-run brasserie in the heart of Bromma serves French-inspired cooking. The nine-page wine list is ambitious for the suburban location; around 20 are available by the glass or as a half-bottle.

title: Den Gyldene Freden
bodyText: Named after the Peace of Nystad in 1721, this historic tavern serves traditional husman in wood-paneled rooms. Owned by the Swedish Academy, it also hosts its customary Thursday dinners.

title: En Liten Krog
bodyText: This intimate dining room serves home cooking with a twist, paired with carefully chosen wines and local craft beers. In summer, the team moves to its coastal sister venue, En Liten Sjökrog.

title: Enoteca Maglia
bodyText: Chef Robert Maglia runs this trattoria with a menu that changes almost daily, backed by a broad selection of Italian wines. An adjoining deli offers curated charcuterie and a range of Italian delicacies.

title: Fei
bodyText: Located on the top floor of the Pier Clarion Hotel in Lindholmen, Fei combines elevated city views with modern Chinese cooking rooted in traditional flavors and a clear sense of authenticity.

title: Frank
bodyText: “Frank Rules” is a four-course menu for which guests choose only the main direction (fish, meat, or vegetarian). The blind format leaves the rest to the kitchen, guided by seasonality and creativity.

title: Hulkoffgården
bodyText: Kurt Hulkoff’s family has farmed by the Torne River since 1721. Since 2005, a converted barn has housed the restaurant, serving organic beef from their own herd and garden-grown produce. Expect mostly Italian wines.

title: Köpmangatan 6
bodyText: In a former bank, two restaurateurs have created a relaxed bistro blending French, Mediterranean, and Swedish flavors. The lively Picklebar and music events complement the food and drinks, especially in summer.

title: Kvarterskrogen Asken
bodyText: Open since 2006, this neighborhood restaurant is named for the ash tree out front. Sommelier Tobias hosts tastings in the cellar, while the enclosed veranda looks onto the cosy Knäppingsborg courtyard.

title: La Fonderie
bodyText: Opened in 2023 in Varvsstaden, restaurateur Stellan Colt runs this French brasserie in a 1910 former casting hall. The wine list favors Burgundy, very fitting for the scenographic interior by designer Mija Kinning.

title: Matateljén
bodyText: In 2025, Henrik Sauer and Anna Klyvare relocated their restaurant to Stockholm’s meatpacking district. Seasonal set menus, served in a raw, industrial dining room, reflect more than a decade of experience at the helm.

title: Melanders Dalagatan
bodyText: Since 1961, Melanders has been a Stockholm institution for seafood. Its outlet in Vasastan pairs a fish counter with a brasserie-style dining room, serving classics like Skagen toast, moules frites, and fish soup.

title: Mellbygatans Restaurang
bodyText: What began as a four-seat deli in 2007 has grown into a restaurant with a selection of over 100 beers. Under chef-owner Emil Årmarker, the kitchen prepares both Swedish and Asian-inspired comfort food.

title: Mestiza
bodyText: True to its name, meaning “mixture”, this social dining spot centers on sharing small plates. Global flavors form a balanced menu, and the popular Basque cheesecake must be pre-ordered.

title: Nabo Matbar
bodyText: Nabo is a neighborhood favorite with a clear wine focus, known for tastings and guest winemaker evenings, alongside seasonal, shareable dishes that let vegetables and flavor take the lead.

title: Norda
bodyText: Marcus Samuelsson brings his Manhattan-meets-Nordic vision to the Clarion Hotel Post. West Coast seafood meets an Oregon-leaning wine cellar and his signature cheddar cheeseburger.

title: Nybrogatan 38
bodyText: Östermalm’s all-day restaurant runs from breakfast through dinner and drinks. Swedish staples form a menu with something for everyone. Nearly 100 wines are listed, with over 50 available by the glass.

title: Ponti
bodyText: Inspired by Italian architect Gio Ponti, this 2025 opening bridges Italy and California. Pizza and grilled dishes meet natural wines, while the bar mixes cocktails with gin, amaro and bitters.

title: Restaurang CG
bodyText: A charcoal grill has defined this steakhouse since 2012. The kitchen dries and marinates meats from both local and international producers, while a recognized cellar focuses on French and Italian wines.

title: Sauvage
bodyText: Sauvage is a much-loved neighborhood bistro led by David Kjellstenius, serving honest, well-crafted cooking where Swedish produce meets French sensibility in a small, warm, and welcoming setting.

title: Segelsalen
bodyText: Inaugurated in 1897 by the Royal Swedish Yacht Club, this dining room serves food inspired by the archipelago. Crayfish dinners in August are a highlight. Sommeliers curate familiar labels and lesser-known bottles.

title: Solen
bodyText: Set in Stockholm’s meatpacking district, Solen is a vibrant dining room shaped by chef-owners Adam Dahlberg and Albin Wessman, known for its cool atmosphere and cosmopolitan cooking.

title: Svartengrens
bodyText: Beef from the archipelago anchors this steakhouse in a former pharmacy. The kitchen smokes its own bacon and pickles vegetables to stretch the seasons, while an award-winning cocktail program rounds out the experience.

title: Tennstopet Grill
bodyText: Tennstopet Grill offers a contemporary take on brasserie dining, where meat, fish, and seafood are cooked over an open grill, balancing elegance with a hearty, international spirit.

title: Bara Vara
bodyText: The name of this corner restaurant since 1999 invites guests to “just be” and relax. Wines age in the cellar, with a focus on France and Italy, and five different Gin & Tonics beg guests to stay after dinner.

title: Bolaget
bodyText: Named for its past as the local alcohol store (Systembolaget), this bistro refines Gotland ingredients with French technique. Tables on the main square invite lingering lunches and unhurried people-watching.

title: Brasserie Greta
bodyText: Owner Sébastien Denie from the Loire Valley brings the taste of his home region to Djursholm. Classics like moules frites and confit de canard are accompanied by over 300 wines and a selection of champagnes.

title: Brasserie Lavette
bodyText: A warm interior sets the tone at this brasserie, which serves classic dishes à la carte and in set menus of three or four courses. French and American wines are available by the glass, including pours via Coravin.

title: Brasserie Makalös
bodyText: Named after a 17th-century palace near Kungsträdgården, this brasserie sits beneath a glass roof in a hotel courtyard. French classics feature on the menu, alongside weekday lunches and relaxed weekend breakfasts.

title: Diket
bodyText: Seven wines are served “on tap” at this neighborhood bar, where curiosity rather than a single cuisine guides the menu. Flavors span widely, with an emphasis on natural choices for drinks.

title: Enoteket
bodyText: An Enomatic system allows guests to pour from 32 wines on display—by the glass, half glass or tasting measure. In the kitchen, a charcoal grill oven turns out sourdough pizza alongside a range of Italian dishes.

title: Far I Hatten
bodyText: Built in 1892, this pavilion in Folkets Park blends food, drinks, and music. Wood-fired pizzas and seasonal dishes pair well with glasses from the strong natural wine list. Mingle among locals on the terrace.

title: Fridas Restaurang
bodyText: Located behind the dunes at Kärradal beach, Fridas has served Scandinavian food since 1988. In summer, live music and the rosé kiosk Krångliga Krabban keep things lively. Sunday lunch buffet most months.

title: Gaia Matbar
bodyText: A weekly choice of five dishes with global accents justifies the trip south of the center to this compact “food bar”. Natural wines change with the menu; reds, whites, and orange wines are available by the glass.

title: Grinda Wärdshus
bodyText: This 1908 island inn has welcomed sailors and summer guests for generations. In the grand dining room, classic archipelago cooking features herring, local fish, and seasonal produce.

title: Häktet
bodyText: At first glance, the former debtors’ prison Bysis (in use 1781–1872) houses a French-Nordic bistro with seasonal cooking. But ring the bell, and the door opens to Vänster, a speakeasy-like cocktail bar.

title: L'Avventura
bodyText: L'Avventura is a lively yet elegant dining room celebrating classic Italian dishes made with premium ingredients, blending tradition with modern flair, and named after L'Avventura, Michelangelo Antonioni’s iconic 1960 film.

title: Pigalle
bodyText: In a converted attic at boutique Hotel Pigalle, this French bistro spreads 1920s glamor with its crystal chandeliers. The open kitchen serves French-inspired plates made from local ingredients. Rooftop terrace.

title: Ransvik Havsveranda
bodyText: Two chefs, Andy and Matti, traded Sweden’s far north for Skåne, opening this seaside café on the Kullaberg peninsula in 2019. A cottage from 1921 frames the food: Swedish classics with a Tuscan touch.

title: Sandy’s
bodyText: Falkenberg Strandbad opened this California-inspired steakhouse in 2022 as a surf ’n’ turf addition to the beach resort. The shared wine selection comes with over 400 listings, primarily French classics.

title: Storgatan 11
bodyText: Fusion cooking brings locals to this compact gastrobar on the historic island of Kvarnholmen. The kitchen blends French and Italian techniques with Asian flavors, supplementing the food with a recognized wine list.

title: The Dining Room
bodyText: Wood-paneled walls, leather chairs, and a backlit bar create a members'-club mood in this 1829 hotel building. The menu features New York-style bistro classics with global touches.

title: vRÅ
bodyText: VRÅ explores the meeting point between Japan and Sweden’s west coast, with a seasonally shifting menu built around seafood and vegetables, defined by clarity, balance, and sustainability.

title: Munkklostret
bodyText: Monks’ dormitories dating to 1384 now house the dining room at this hotel in a former monastery. The kitchen uses seasonal and preserved ingredients from the region. Wines are kept in the medieval cellar.

title: Hambergs
bodyText: Since 1982, the Hamberg family has supplied this white-tiled fish restaurant with seafood from France and vegetables from their own island garden. No-fuss cooking puts the ingredients in the spotlight.

title: På Skissernas
bodyText: Located within Skissernas Museum, this restaurant serves a thoughtfully composed menu rooted in local produce from both sea and land, while daytime lunches take on a more relaxed, casual feel.

title: Smakrike Krog
bodyText: Producers from all over Gotland supply this restaurant, located in a former trading house from the 1860s. Tasting menus are served on the glass-enclosed veranda. Six hotel rooms are available; summer season only.

title: Tegelbacken
bodyText: Tegelbacken is a modern brasserie in the city center, known for seasonal, Mediterranean-inspired cooking with contemporary finesse, a strong wine program, and a relaxed yet polished evening atmosphere.

title: Bobergs på Hamngården
bodyText: At Bobergs på Hamngården, seasonal, locally rooted cuisine meets creative, globally inspired tasting menus in a historic seaside setting, with panoramic harbor views and standout wines.

title: Bacchanale
bodyText: A convivial restaurant inspired by Southern Europe, Bacchanale focuses on seasonal produce and a wine-driven menu, guided by a sure touch and complemented by a pleasant outdoor terrace.

title: Bar Europa
bodyText: Natural wine on tap and Mediterranean small plates reward the journey to this compact bar near the Folkoperan, where the menu arrives printed like a receipt, with terrace seating waiting for warmer days.

title: Bastardo
bodyText: “Crossbreed” refers to three Swedish restaurateurs—Jesper Skemark, Daniel Gunneriusson, and Joakim Mering Andersson—bringing Italian cooking to an 18th-century inn, centered on handmade pasta and natural wines.

title: Bergamott
bodyText: Escargots, steak tartare, and the signature horse fillet are favorites at this bistro that feels as if taken from a side street in Paris. Just like the food, the wine list is French, and the staff speak the language too.

title: Bikt
bodyText: Bearing the name “confession” and located opposite the Cathedral, this lively spot wanders the kitchens of France, Spain, and Italy. Two inner courtyards open in summer, and the kitchen stays busy from lunch until late.

title: Bombance Bistrot & Boucherie
bodyText: Chef Johan Beckman and his wife, Britt-Marie Edström, spent 20 years running restaurants in Chamonix and Fayence. Back in Sweden, they opened this authentic bistro with 32 seats and a French atmosphere.

title: Bräjks Matbar
bodyText: Where the pistes Björnstigen and Långsvängen split, this timber-clad lunch restaurant prioritizes homemade cooking over convenience food. The kitchen uses Swedish ingredients for meatballs and other classics.

title: Den Lilla Krogen
bodyText: Truffles from nearby Gudhem, seasonal game, and Iberico pork from Spain dot the menu at this restaurant in Skövde, known for weekday lunches and ambitious dinners. The wine list features plenty from Piedmont.

title: En Liten Sjökrog
bodyText: Sea views stretch to the horizon at this summer restaurant on the coast of Hälsingland. The kitchen celebrates northern ingredients such as moose, char, Kalix bleak roe, and reindeer from Arvidsjaur.

title: Främmat
bodyText: A restaurant where classical French foundations meet a playful, experimental mindset. Expect confident cooking, unexpected combinations, and an atmosphere that feels both energetic and welcoming.

title: Grano gbg
bodyText: Brothers Thomas and Christoffer Sjögren opened their restaurant in 2018, offering both pizza and tasting menus. The name plays on Granö in Norrland (where their parents met) and the Italian word for wheat.

title: Gro
bodyText: Rebranded in 2020 in the cobbled Stallbacken courtyard, this climate-conscious restaurant puts organic ingredients at the center. À la carte and two tasting menus are available, one of which is vegan.

title: Hattmakarn Brasserie & Bar
bodyText: Opened in 2024 and named after the historic quarter of hatmakers, this restaurant is run by three chefs from established kitchens. Modern Swedish-French cuisine is served in a space that flows seamlessly into a bar.

title: Hemma
bodyText: Owner Jonny Lundberg runs this yellow timber house, where food has been served since 1875. The kitchen prepares its own stocks, bakes bread, makes pasta, and churns ice cream in-house. Courtyard seating in summer.

title: Indio Kitchen
bodyText: Sweden's first Nikkei restaurant brings Japanese-Peruvian fusion to Kocksgatan, literally “Chefs' Street.” Precise sushi meets ceviche, with pisco cocktails at the bar. Counter seats let guests watch the chefs at work.

title: JH matbar
bodyText: A modern Scandinavian restaurant by Christoffer and Malin Jedenstam, where relaxed yet refined cooking is served in an inviting atmosphere for locals and visitors alike, on Ystad’s main street.

title: Kajplats 9
bodyText: Set in the former customs house by the harbor since 2012, this brasserie looks out over Lake Mälaren. Fish, shellfish and Swedish “husman” are served throughout the year, while the ice cream bar opens in summer.

title: Kitchenette
bodyText: Guests are encouraged to start by sharing two or three dishes for two people to explore flavors together. Once satisfied, the focus shifts to a single, substantial meat course meant for the table.

title: Långbro Världshus
bodyText: Housed in a historic villa in Älvsjö, Långbro Värdshus is led by Fredrik Eriksson, offering seasonal, sustainably minded cooking rooted in Swedish tradition with influences from other countries.

title: Monrads
bodyText: Since 2007, Lina and Johan Monrad have run their Djursholm outpost, combining a seafood counter with a brasserie-style dining room. Swedish and French classics are paired with a solid wine selection.

title: Namu
