bodyText: Adopted from South Korea and raised in Sweden, TV chef Jennie Walldén reconnects with her roots through food at Namu—Korean for “tree”. Artfully plated dishes blend Asian flavors with locally sourced produce.

title: Napolyon Bistro & Bar
bodyText: French bistro classics with a Swedish accent: Since 2012, the kitchen has served bouillabaisse, beef tartare, and daily fish. Window tables offer people-watching on one of Östermalm’s busiest pedestrian streets.

title: Nous Bistro
bodyText: After gaining recognition at GIN, Stefan Johansson and Oliver Kördel opened this follow-up in 2023. French technique meets ingredients from Östergötland in a relaxed and contemporary dining room.

title: Pescadores
bodyText: Fishing runs in the Haglund family, since Hans’s grandfather worked in the Västervik archipelago. He and his son Viktor opened this seafood restaurant in 2011 in a cozy, nautical setting.

title: Prospero
bodyText: Defined by restraint and precision, Prospero offers a concise, seasonally changing menu where small plates are built around clarity of flavor and ingredients chosen strictly at their peak.

title: Smaca
bodyText: The open kitchen shows how dishes made with seasonal, locally sourced ingredients are prepared. Julia selects drink pairings to match the food. With exposed brick and candlelight, the dining room feels warm and cosy.

title: Tizne
bodyText: Tizne presents a refined yet soulful take on Mexican cooking, where comforting dishes are shaped by traditional flavors, contemporary technique, and a clear respect for culinary heritage.

title: Tosto
bodyText: In-house charcuterie, slow-aged meat and even fish, alongside hand-rolled pasta, headline this Italian-leaning newcomer from Max Duhs, opened in 2025, with a wine list that champions lesser-known grape varieties.

title: Uppströms Fisk & Skaldjur
bodyText: Carl Andreasson opened this refined seafood spot in 2018. Despite being located in the Kvarnengallerian shopping mall, the room feels sophisticated thanks to white fish-scale tiles and stylized drawings.

title: Wasahof
bodyText: Run by the Holmberg-Cornelius family since 1968, this seafood bistro is now in its fourth generation. Head chef Fredrik prepares seafood platters and lobster, while brother Patrik manages the cellar.

title: Aaltos
bodyText: In a 1965 building designed by Alvar Aalto, a stylish restaurant with marble and greenery awaits. The Finnish master loved Italy, and this grill honors the connection with its wide choice of comfort food.

title: Aubergine
bodyText: Truffle weeks in November and December are an annual highlight for regulars at this bistro. Otherwise, guests enjoy Franco-Swedish cooking with Italian touches in an intimate yet stylish space.

title: Baldersnäs Kök
bodyText: Located on a peninsula in Lake Laxsjön, this manor is surrounded by an English park from the 19th century, now a nature reserve. Ingredients come from an on-site herb garden and producers in Dalsland.

title: Bar Nîmes
bodyText: An inviting bistro blending French and Italian influences, Bar Nîmes offers generous flavors in a warm, bustling setting, shaped by Kim Öhman's relaxed yet lively approach to hospitality.

title: Bara Vin & Bistro
bodyText: Bara Vin & Bistro on Kristianstad’s main street is a small restaurant with serious wine credentials. Carefully selected bottles and well-chosen wines by the glass are paired with French classics in a relaxed, welcoming setting.

title: BISe
bodyText: Restaurant, wine bar, and cocktail bar share one roof at this newcomer spot, opened in 2022. Wines from small vineyards pair well with Ludvig Fredriksson’s eclectic cooking, rooted in Southern Europe.

title: Bistro Arsenalen
bodyText: This French-oriented bistro is known for its tartare and truffle pasta. Inside, it radiates a classic Parisian style with patterned tile floors, dark green leather banquettes, large mirrors, and chandeliers.

title: Bjerreds Saltsjöbad Kallbadhus & Restaurang
bodyText: Walk 574 meters along one of Sweden's longest piers to reach this cold-bathhouse restaurant, rebuilt in 2004. The cooking is elevated by panoramic views over the Öresund. Popular brunch on weekends.

title: Brasserie Balzac
bodyText: Named after oyster lover Honoré de Balzac, this brasserie sources from small French producers for classic dishes reflecting the country’s diversity. An opulent interior and long cocktail bar frame the experience.

title: Brasserie Sture 1912
bodyText: This brasserie pairs a refined, continental setting with a spirited, convivial mood, serving classic dishes in a space made for both everyday meals and celebratory occasions, seven days a week.

title: Bryggeriet Ångkvarn
bodyText: At Uppsala's first brewpub, hearty dishes are prepared with meat from regional suppliers. The name traces to a steam mill founded in 1874, and beer tastings are held twice monthly on Saturdays.

title: Café Klotet
bodyText: Since 2024, this relaxed restaurant has served seasonal bistro dishes with rustic touches. Floor-to-ceiling windows frame views over Slussen, giving the airy dining room a strong sense of place.

title: Café Nizza
bodyText: Rooted in classic bistro tradition, Café Nizza takes a quietly confident approach to cooking, letting seasonal produce, thoughtful flavors, and an expansive wine list set the tone.

title: Elsa
bodyText: Chef Leon Boström runs this relaxed canal-side spot near Malmöhus Castle. Globally inspired dishes are paired with natural wines, while sustainability shapes the kitchen’s thoughtful use of seasonal produce.

title: Elviras Skärgårdskrog
bodyText: Reached by ferry from Almö, this seasonal restaurant sits on the island of Lilla Brattön. The kitchen refines ingredients from nearby waters and farms, including langoustines from Mollösund. Archipelago views.

title: Enoclub Osteria
bodyText: Near the lively Lilla Torg square, this family-run osteria spans two floors. It pours wines sourced directly from Italy and hosts tastings. The kitchen prepares risotto, vitello tonnato and other classics.

title: Fabriksköket
bodyText: Set in an 1833 cotton mill on Lake Sävelången, the “factory kitchen” serves dishes based on Swedish meat and produce from nearby farms. Seasonal set menus are available exclusively to hotel guests.

title: Fårögården
bodyText: This farmstead pairs a B&B in a school from 1850 with a restaurant in a converted stable. Gotlandic–Mediterranean dishes are served along with coffee and gelato, enjoyed outdoors unless the weather turns.

title: Fejan restaurant
bodyText: Hotelier Pelle Lydmar runs this seasonal archipelago outpost on Fejan, an island reached only by boat. Mediterranean-influenced seafood fills the menu, paired with sweeping sea views.

title: Fina Fisken
bodyText: Since 1974, this “fine fish” has prepared maritime treasures for summer visitors. Warm evenings draw guests to the garden, and the long list of wines and beers keeps them there. Wine & dine evenings off-season.

title: Fjällpuben
bodyText: Opened in 2008 by TV chefs Markus Aujalay and Melker Andersson, this cozy ski-village spot serves Arctic char, reindeer, and roe in Jämtland style. Embroidered hangings and rag rugs line the walls.

title: Guldapan
bodyText: Ingredients from Värmland meet a weekly updated wine list at this bistro bar. Charcuterie, oysters, and seafood arrive on carefully arranged plates, part of a menu shaped by international influences.

title: John's Place
bodyText: Since 1970, this weathered beach house has cooked over a charcoal grill close to the sea. Steaks are prepared on open flames, and regulars return for the classics and the familiar atmosphere.

title: Ma Cuisine
bodyText: Ma Cuisine is a family-run French bistro in central Gothenburg, serving classic dishes cooked from scratch with seasonal Swedish produce, thoughtfully paired with a wine list rich in French gems.

title: Pålsjö krog
bodyText: The KOL & Cocktails group took over this institution beside the historic Pålsjö cold bath in 2024, keeping the focus on seafood and Swedish classics. Summer brings after-beach evenings and boule on the terrace.

title: Skanshof
bodyText: A former bank was transformed into a four-floor venue blending gastronomy and gallery space. A rooftop garden with bar and pool tops the building, while the bistro serves seafood and classic dishes with a New York twist.

title: Skivarps Gästgivaregård
bodyText: This historic inn, with roots in the 1680s, is run by Jeanette and Johan Bohman. Scanian classics highlight local produce, while Wine & Dine events explore regions through tastings and discoveries by the glass.

title: The Hills
bodyText: Opened in 2019, this Swedish-French bistro features an interior of solid wood and leather banquettes created by Swedish designer Jonas Bohlin. The compact menu offers classics at both lunch and dinner.

title: Astrids
bodyText: The locals in the suburb of Bromma come here to welcome the weekend with wine and food. French-inspired dishes like entrecôte and fish soup taste best on the terrace beside the Bauhaus villas of Södra Ängby.

title: Bistro Perspektiv
bodyText: Sommelier Frida Ringström runs this beachside bistro within the Falsterbo Photo Art Museum. French and Nordic influences drive the kitchen, which operates only in the summer. Off-season café on weekends.

title: Grand Italian
bodyText: Perched on the 25th floor of Clarion Hotel Malmö Live, this Italian dining room boasts views over the city and the Öresund. The open kitchen serves Italian classics, while the sky bar pours cocktails.

title: Vina
bodyText: Sisters Lina and Julia Lundström run this relaxed gastrobar, pouring natural wines from small European producers. The kitchen serves dishes like beef tartare and fish soup across two floors.

title: Bruksrestaurangen
bodyText: Trained at Noma and The Fat Duck, chef Axel Johnsson brought fine-dining ambition to Hälleforsnäs Bruk, an ironworks founded in 1659, once dubbed Sweden's most boring town.

title: Kin Long
bodyText: With golden dragons, a lattice ceiling, and plenty of red, the oldest Chinese restaurant in Malmö transports guests straight to the Celestial Empire. Authentic cooking since 1964, offering hot pot and tasting menus.

title: Lyran
bodyText: Lyran offers a carefully composed tasting menu where standout ingredients and their producers lead the narrative, highlighting origin, craftsmanship, and seasonality throughout the experience.

title: Ricordi
bodyText: Designed by London-based Chalk Architects, Ricordi opened in 2021 with vintage glamor. Fresh pasta and sourdough pizza are served across three rooms with bold ceiling art by Malin Gabriella Nordin.

title: Sill & Dynamit
bodyText: The kitchen uses ingredients from forests, waters, and farms around Lake Vänern, while the beer is brewed in their own nearby brewery. In summer, tables fill the terrace overlooking Mariestad’s guest harbor.

title: Tivedens Mat
bodyText: Known as “Krogen mitt i skogen” (the pub in the forest), this barn restaurant has served French-Swedish cooking from a chalkboard menu for two decades. Craft beer complements the wine list. Summer only.

title: Varvet
bodyText: Tomas Diederichsen, Chef of the Year 2011, cooks at this summer-only archipelago restaurant set in a former boatyard workshop. Four guest rooms and a small on-site shop make it easy to stay longer.

title: Ångbryggeriet
bodyText: Chef Mari Wigren opened in 2016 in a former brewery after trading football in Norway for a career in the kitchen. Her cooking celebrates Norrbotten’s specialties like Arctic char and moose tartare. Deli attached.

title: Banken Bar & Brasserie
bodyText: Opened in 1988 in a turn-of-the-century bank building, this French-inspired brasserie retains Jugend lamps, red sofas, and a sister delicatessen nearby. Classics are made with moose entrecôte and MSC-certified fish.

title: Barbro
bodyText: Andrew Jones and Tim Alton, both Yasuragi alumni, opened this Asian-fusion restaurant under the Liljeholmen bridge in 2011. Dishes made with Nordic ingredients are served in a dark room with bold artwork.

title: Bazar Bar & Restaurang
bodyText: Brothers Mattias and Andreas Olsson created this lively venue on the harbor, known for meat dishes, Neapolitan pizza, and a modern wine list. Head chef Therese works with a charcoal grill and low-temperature aging.

title: Brasserie Bardot
bodyText: In homage to Brigitte Bardot, this French brasserie opened in 2024. The space seats around 60 guests and pairs classic French cooking with an atmosphere the owners describe as a luxurious living room. Dinner only.

title: Brogatan
bodyText: The team behind restaurant Riket revived this bistro classic, where French techniques are applied to Swedish ingredients. The front bar buzzes with after-work energy, while the inner dining room stays intimate.

title: Broms
bodyText: After years of basement catering, Anna Bauer's sunny corner bistro has become a beloved neighborhood hub. Dining room and deli run all day, from breakfast to lunch, dinner, and evening drinks.

title: Djäknebergets Restaurang
bodyText: Brothers Jiri and Tommy Ondracek run this panoramic restaurant overlooking Västerås and Lake Mälaren. Swedish classics are reworked in the kitchen, with zander from Lake Hjälmaren as a signature ingredient.

title: Enkai
bodyText: Since 2022, this Hornstull izakaya has served ramen at lunch and charcoal-grilled skewers in the evening. The omakase menu with sake pairing features dishes from a single chicken, showing its versatility.

title: Fågelboet
bodyText: Housed in one of Sälen’s oldest buildings, dating from the 17th century, this intimate restaurant by the slopes is run by the Siwersons. Game fondue with reindeer or moose is the speciality, while a fireplace adds welcome warmth.

title: Familjen
bodyText: A modern bistro with a distinctly homely feel, where contemporary ideas meet comfort-driven cooking. Local, seasonal ingredients, cocktails, and a lively, social atmosphere set the tone.

title: Gambrinus
bodyText: The bistro at Grand Hotel has been a culinary institution for generations. It celebrates Skåne’s fertile farmland by using regional produce to create classic dishes. The wine cellar stocks many older vintages.

title: GT Villan
bodyText: At this sister restaurant to Krusmyntagården, modern and classic influences meet herbs picked from the garden. The terrace faces the sea, making it a summer-only destination for lingering sunset dinners.

title: Gujju
bodyText: Nikhil and Varsha Mistry bring the flavors of India to western Sweden, taking guests on a culinary journey across their vast homeland. Dishes are available in whole and half portions for maximum variety.

title: Kanon
bodyText: Charcoal grilling is central at this 2024 newcomer. In an already restaurant-dense corner of Södermalm, it adds Middle Eastern, Mediterranean, and South American flavors and dishes to the mix.

title: Lola Maria
bodyText: Opened in multicultural Malmö in 2025, this restaurant reflects Andalusia's layered influences. Polish-born chef Tomasz Barański, trained in London, reinterprets classic Spanish flavors in a vibrant setting.

title: Matilda
bodyText: Set on the photogenic Ingrid Bergman Square, this restaurant is part of the Bryggan hotel complex. The menu focuses on fish and seafood, served right by the water with views out toward the archipelago.

title: Matscenen
bodyText: “Chokladboll & Champagne” is the motto at this bistro inside a theater from 1901, where small plates, Swedish classics, and cocktails take center stage. In summer, guests can play boules in the park beside the terrace.

title: Palmers
bodyText: Mediterranean cuisine and a charcoal grill define this resort-hotel restaurant at the far end of Lidingö Island. The menu is inspired by the Greek archipelago, Moroccan food markets, and Lebanese meze traditions.

title: Paraden Kvarterskrog & Bar
bodyText: The Paraden cinema opened in 1932 and screened films for nearly five decades. Today, it houses a neighborhood restaurant, serving comfort food on two levels. The guests upstairs overlook the open kitchen.

title: Pelles Rökeri Grundsund
bodyText: Despite its name, this is not a smokehouse but a seasonal seafood restaurant highlighting fish from Bohuslän. Tables sit meters from the sea, with evenings often continuing at Hugo's Bu in a 1905 boathouse.

title: PW Kök & Bar
bodyText: Olympic ski champion Pernilla Wiberg lends her initials to this hotel restaurant with ski-in access. The kitchen uses local Dalarna ingredients, from char to reindeer, served in classic dishes with a contemporary edge.

title: Shibumi
bodyText: Sayan Isaksson pioneered the izakaya genre in Stockholm when he opened Shibumi (meaning “effortless perfection”) in 2015. Reopened in 2025, this subterranean spot serves sharing plates with cocktails, sake, and shochu.

title: Tengu
bodyText: Opened in 2021 with chef Jonas Lindgren involved, this ramen-focused spot serves slow-simmered shoyu, shio, and miso bowls. Small plates come off the grill, with sake and Japanese beer enjoyed at the relaxed counter.

title: The Lamp Restaurant
bodyText: What first meets the eye at this hotel restaurant is Sweden’s largest table lamp, towering over the dining room. Nordic produce meets Asian technique, and a Feng Shui-inspired courtyard opens in summer.

title: Veto
bodyText: Comfort food with Mediterranean flavors, designed to make people happy—that's the promise at this laid-back neighborhood restaurant. A wine list of personal favorites encourages guests to try something new.

title: Barabicu
bodyText: Mediterranean and Levantine meze meant for sharing are prepared over an open flame. The whole suckling pig feeds six, but must be ordered two days ahead. The summer terrace overlooks the Rosenlund canal.

title: Brasseriet Tack o Bock
bodyText: Robin Jansson and Kristin Granström run this brasserie, where beer is brewed in-house, and the kitchen refines ingredients from Öland. The drinks program contains over 50 beers, a cocktail bar, and an extensive wine list.

title: Cantina N3
bodyText: Graziano Janmichele from Sicily set up this wine bar to bring authentic Italian food culture to Örebro. Expect seasonal cooking and handmade pasta, with ingredients sourced from Italian producers.

title: Dolcetto
bodyText: Quality ingredients and straightforward cooking define this Italian trattoria, inspired by village food. Guests can opt for a self-guided tasting of four wines, using the restaurant’s own materials.

title: Hos Talevski Stadsparken
bodyText: This restaurant with a wine room in the city park welcomes locals and visitors for wood-fired pizzas and a sharing-focused menu. The Talevski family has developed the interior with leather, solid oak, and warm tones.

title: Il Forno Italiano
bodyText: Wood-fired pizza and fresh pasta have made this Tuscan-style trattoria a local favorite since 2003. The wine list focuses on family-owned estates from across Italy, and winemaker dinners are regularly on the calendar.

title: Kackelstugan
bodyText: Founded by Gunnar Aldestam and Agneta Ringman, Kackelstugan grew from informal gatherings into a restaurant in 1997. A courtyard, live music, and a microbrewery have made it one of Öland's summer destinations.

title: Knarrholmens Restaurang
bodyText: On a car-free island, just 15 minutes by ferry from Gothenburg, this archipelago restaurant opened in 2017. Seasonal cooking and regular winemakers’ dinners reward the journey. Outdoor seating, mainly in summer.

title: Västervik
bodyText: Created by ABBA's Björn Ulvaeus in his childhood town, this waterfront hotel-restaurant blends Småland ingredients with global influences. All dishes are prepared in an open kitchen at its center.

title: Bistro Odette
bodyText: Run by sommelier Emma Wennerberg and chef Mathias Graner, Bistro Odette is a warm homage to French classics—seasonal, rustic yet refined, with a much-loved tarte flambée among the signatures.

title: Botanico
bodyText: Latin American and Asian flavors meet in this dark, jungle-inspired space, where sharing plates run from tuna tartare and ceviche to bao buns and tropical-leaning sushi. A downstairs cocktail bar keeps the night going.

title: B.A.R.
bodyText: A refined seafood restaurant, B.A.R. is known for pristine fish and shellfish, classic technique, and a buzzy dining room, while also offering some well-crafted meat dishes for those who prefer them.

title: Bakfickan
bodyText: For over 25 years, this fish-and-seafood spot in a small house beside the ruins of St. Karin’s church has delivered on fried Baltic herring and fish soup. The dishes pair well with beer from Gotlands Bryggeri.

title: Nomad
bodyText: Swedish classics are prepared from scratch at this dog-friendly food bar. The short menu always includes meatballs with lingonberries, as well as game dishes featuring elk, reindeer, and deer.

title: Udden Japanese Cuisine
bodyText: Fusion-style sushi adapted for European tastes, with bold presentations and high-quality fish. The kitchen balances traditional techniques with creative combinations across nigiri, ramen, and tonkatsu.

title: Woodstockholm
bodyText: Woodstockholm centers on creative, ingredient-driven cooking, known for playful, seasonally themed menus, paired with wine from smaller producers with high standards of sustainability.

title: Aristo
bodyText: A bistro defined by genuine hospitality, assured cooking, and well-defined flavors, Aristo focuses on seasonal produce and classic technique, delivering a relaxed yet well-composed experience.

title: Collage
bodyText: Chef Stefan Karlsson leads this lively brasserie in a historic building that once housed a cigar factory and a porcelain shop. Expect classics like steak frites, beef tartare, and generous seafood platters.

title: Dersch
bodyText: Schnitzel takes center stage at Roy Nader’s restaurant, where veal, Iberico pork, and turbot arrive crisp, fried in butter. Sides and flavors draw on Austrian tradition, handled with a modern touch.

title: Edvalls Guld
bodyText: Provence meets Norrland at this brasserie in Sundsvall’s Stenstan, a district rebuilt in stone after a fire in 1888. The lively kitchen hosts seasonal events, such as jazz brunches and themed dinners.

title: Invito
bodyText: Self-described as a “people’s fine-dining spot,” this central address pairs Italian cooking with Norrland produce. The wine cellar hosts tastings, and Thursday pizza nights are just as popular as the weekday lunch service.

title: Lilla Styrbjörn
bodyText: Old family recipes are at the heart of the menu at this gastropub, where Swedish staples like blood pudding and hand-rolled meatballs are offered alongside moules frites and oysters. Craft beer and music after dark.

title: Lilla Vildt
bodyText: Part restaurant, part deli counter, this “little wild” mountain-village spot stocks cheeses and charcuterie alongside a menu of mid-sized plates. Northern ingredients, such as cured reindeer, feature on the menu.

title: Mäster Anders
bodyText: On a cold winter day in 1692, Anders Månsson Holm opened his inn on Kungsholmen. Keeping the name, it moved to Pipersgatan in 1905. Yellow-tiled walls, wooden furniture and the patterned floor remain from that time.

title: Mr P
bodyText: Named after Pontus Fürstenberg, whose art collection was donated to the museum next door, this brasserie serves globally influenced sharing plates. In summer, a large terrace opens onto Götaplatsen.

title: Sandhamns Värdshus
bodyText: In summer, boats reach Sandhamn from central Stockholm in just over two hours. The island's main inn dates back to 1672 and serves Swedish classics in a yellow timber house overlooking the harbor.

title: Spanjorskan
bodyText: Is it a backstreet bar in Madrid or a neighborhood spot in Östermalm? “The Spanish Lady” pairs charcuterie of Iberico pork and Galician beef with tapas served in rounds. Weekday lunches offer a Spanish buffet.

title: Vita Duvan
bodyText: Three siblings who also run two historic hotels in Marstrand opened the wood-panelled “White Dove” in 2024, honoring their uncles’ 1960s club with a similar name. The menu lists sole, entrecôte, raw beef, and more.

title: Åsbogatan 1
bodyText: In this bistro on one of Borås’s liveliest streets, the kitchen is inspired by Italy and France, with small plates designed for sharing. European wines and house cocktails, plus a sun-filled summer terrace.

title: Balthazar
bodyText: Indoor boule courts share an address with this bistro on the Viskan River. The kitchen mixes French and Swedish influences: oysters, steak tartare, a signature burger. Bakery attached; open since 2018.

title: Bistrot Paname
bodyText: Michel and Noël run this hideaway where Parisian chansons play, and staff speak French among themselves. The tiny room fills with expats and locals seeking boeuf bourguignon, escargots, and cider.

title: Bockholmen Hav & Restaurang
bodyText: Bockholmen Hav & Restaurang pairs classic Swedish flavors with seasonal produce and international touches, served in a tranquil waterfront setting with warm hospitality and elegance.

title: Boqueria
bodyText: Opened in December 2020, this is the third outpost of the Stockholm-based Boqueria group. The tapas, made with Mediterranean specialities, are accompanied by a recognized, Spain-focused wine list.

title: Boqueria Åre
bodyText: Part of the Boqueria Group with several locations, this après-ski destination brings tapas close to the slopes. The menu features charcoal-grilled peppers, Galician beef, and Spanish cheeses like Manchego and La Peral.

title: Faccia Grassa
bodyText: Chef-owner Johan Blomberg channels Bologna's pasta traditions, serving hand-rolled pasta shaped with precision and soul. Expect deep flavors, impeccable textures and fillings that truly shine.

title: Hestraviken Restaurang
bodyText: The River Nissan flows past this group of early 1900s timber villas. Regional ingredients are prepared with Swedish and Mediterranean influences, served in small dining rooms overlooking Lake Algustorpasjön.

title: Hornsgatan Kvarterskrog & Bar
bodyText: A long bar stretches from the open kitchen to a seafood counter, while the cellar contains flavored spirits developed in-house under its own label. Swedish and Mediterranean influences result in honest, unfussy dishes.

title: Pom Friterie
bodyText: Dutch founders Marvin Romein and Jorit Gras spent several years refining their fries before opening their minimalist place. The potatoes come from a single grower on the North Sea coast.

title: Ruths
bodyText: Since opening in 2021, this modern bistro has run from morning coffee and homemade pastries through to dinner without changing gear. The open kitchen prepares Mediterranean dishes, often paired with natural wines.

title: Kukkolaforsen Restaurang
bodyText: Six generations of the Spolander family have run this restaurant overlooking Kukkolaforsen, the largest rapid on the Torne River. Dishes follow the traditions of an area with Swedish-Finnish heritage.

title: Bullen
bodyText: On Storgatan in Malmö, Restaurang Bullen ranks among the city’s oldest beer halls, pouring pilsner and serving classic Swedish fare since 1897 in a time-capsule setting steeped in 1960s charm and loyal regulars.

title: Musselbaren
bodyText: Housed in a 19th-century clock tower, this restaurant is devoted to blue mussels from nearby farms. From April to October, guests can join boat trips to the fjord to harvest mussels before dinner.

title: Bistro Süd
bodyText: Journalists and artists have gathered at this institution for over two decades. The kitchen is strong on farm cheeses, tartare, and a popular burger, while the Gino dessert was adopted from sister restaurant PA & Co.

title: Fiore
bodyText: Leaf-patterned wallpaper, bentwood chairs, and a long bar counter define this polished bistro. Italian dishes dominate the menu, while desserts remain creatively Nordic. Chocolate from the house plantation in Tobago.

title: Jernberghska
bodyText: Inside a smithy from 1650 at the local open-air museum, this atmospheric spot serves traditional Swedish, German, French, and Austrian dishes. The concept has been refreshed under new ownership since 2025.

title: Smak pa Restaurangen
bodyText: Smak offers a relaxed take on fine dining, where guests shape their own tasting menu by choosing the number of courses, each built around a single, carefully selected main ingredient.

title: Söderköpings Brunn
bodyText: Just a short walk from the Göta Canal lies one of Sweden’s oldest spa establishments, where guests have enjoyed the healing waters since 1719. The restaurant serves seasonal Swedish dinners and weekday lunches.

title: Strandpiren
bodyText: Seafood leads at this hotel restaurant overlooking the water and town’s largest summer terrace. Fish and shellfish dominate the menu, with char, mussels and occasional lobster specials.

title: torgEtt
bodyText: Skiers and hikers gather after a day on the slopes for tapas-style small plates and à la carte dishes. A fireplace warms the dining room in winter, and a terrace opens in summer for outdoor seating.

title: Bleck
bodyText: Founder Kalle Schröder turned a former tool shed into a neighborhood favorite in 2015. The compact spot offers a small menu with vegetarian options, plus year-round weekend brunch and daily summer service.

title: TB Grill Room
bodyText: At Sälens Högfjällshotell, an American-style steakhouse allows guests to choose cut, cooking method, and sides. The hotel is also known for its extensive wine and Champagne collection.

title: Varggransstugan
bodyText: Perched about 900 meters above sea level, this cabin welcomes skiers and snowmobilers. A new generation now leads the kitchen, serving Swedish-French cooking with subtle Sámi touches.

title: Strandvägen 1
bodyText: Next door to the Royal Dramatic Theater, this all-day bistro fills with locals and visitors alike. The kitchen offers classic European dishes, while the terrace is a popular spot on warm summer days.

title: 800 grader
bodyText: Four pizzas, no more. The wood-fired oven runs at 800°C, turning thin dough into rounds with crisp edges, topped with fior di latte and San Marzano. One more location in trendy Midsommarkransen.

title: Spill
bodyText: Former Daniel Berlin Krog chefs Erik Andersson Mohlin and Ellinor Lindblom Mohlin rescue surplus ingredients and turn them into two daily lunch dishes, served in a modern canteen with communal tables.

title: Surfers Visby
bodyText: Sichuan-inspired cooking meets a kitschy South Pacific beach bar. Small plates of dan dan noodles, mapo tofu, dumplings, and five-spice ribs are designed for sharing and go well with the fruity cocktails.

title: Ai Ramen Sofia
bodyText: Stockholm’s first ramen bar opened in 2015 and was named the best budget restaurant the following year. The kitchen serves rich pork and chicken broths with house noodles and Japanese-style toppings.

title: Nationalmuseum Restaurang
bodyText: Run by Fredrik Eriksson, adviser to the Nobel Foundation, this museum restaurant is shaped by Swedish designers. Lunch spotlights contemporary Nordic cooking served counter-style, while Glasbaren opens from 11.

title: Tennstopet
bodyText: Tennstopet is a long-standing Stockholm institution devoted to traditional Swedish cooking, where hearty, time-honored dishes are served in a setting rich with history and old-world character.

title: Cadierbaren
bodyText: Everyone is welcome at "Cadierbaren" - from discerning Stockholmers to hotel guests passing through. This grand, glamorous bar is equally suitable for after-work meetings, informal get-togethers or lively evenings with champagne and creative cocktails. Don't hesitate to challenge the bartenders: they are among the best in Sweden.

title: Le Hibou at Bank Hotel
bodyText: Perched high above Stockholm, "Le Hibou" offers more than just a breathtaking view - it offers an intimate, upscale cocktail experience. The elegant yet inviting rooftop bar is known for its perfectly balanced drinks and expert bartenders, who add a sense of craftsmanship and distinction to every visit.

title: Othilia
bodyText: This innovative bar, the result of a partnership between "A Bar Called Gemma" and "Operakällaren", combines gastronomy and mixology in perfect harmony. Class, creativity and inclusivity come together in an elegant, timeless setting, creating an atmosphere that is as refined as it is dynamic.

title: Stjärtilleriet
bodyText: An experimental, art-focused cocktail bar where design, playfulness and taste merge in perfect balance. Cocktails are prepared here with theatrical flair - ideal for anyone looking for an experience that is as distinctive as it is unforgettable.

title: Bar Bruno
bodyText: A relaxed retreat where pleasant moments, shared experiences and warm hospitality come together.

title: A bar called Gemma
bodyText: This chic cocktail bar in Östermalm is a cozy retreat known for its creative yet wonderfully balanced drinks. Thanks to imaginative signature drinks, a warm, welcoming atmosphere and a subtle international flair, it has quickly become a popular meeting place since opening in 2019 - even among industry insiders.

title: Tjoget
bodyText: This popular bar in Hornstull is known for its Mediterranean flair, energy, cultural mix and award-winning drinks. The atmosphere is warm and informal - a place where creativity meets craftsmanship and quality goes hand in hand with genuine conviviality.

title: Bar Afterglow
bodyText: A lively "Grätzel bar" where playful mixology meets casual charm. Creative cocktails are served in an inviting atmosphere - and sometimes shared with four-legged friends - making the bar the perfect place for a relaxed evening with character and style.

title: 20hundra5
bodyText: A retro-charming cocktail bar with a cosy, lively spirit, featuring classic video games and subtly evocative touches. Creative cocktails and a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere make it an inviting choice for a night out with a hint of old-school charm.

title: MAP Petite Maison
bodyText: A cultivated Stockholm cocktail bar where premium spirits meet artful mixology. Here, impeccably crafted drinks sit alongside curated artworks, atmospheric music and elevated small plates, coming together to create a sophisticated, multi-sensory experience.

title: Care/of Cocktailbar
bodyText: This acclaimed Malmö cocktail bar has earned a long-standing place among Sweden’s finest. Celebrated for its reliability and warm hospitality, it offers impeccably balanced drinks alongside a seasonal line-up of inventive new serves, and for a touch of playful charm, some of the city’s best hot dogs.

title: Bar Brahe
bodyText: Once upon a time, on the fringe of the Old Town, a discreet harbour-side alley served as a gathering point for merchants collecting bricks and coffee for export. Today, the legacy of that historic trading warehouse endures, its character subtly infused into the walls of Bar Brahe, an elegant jazz-and-cocktail bar that reimagines the past with quiet sophistication.

title: Pharmarium
bodyText: A cocktail bar in the Old Town inspired by history, where the legacy of an old pharmacy meets contemporary mixology. The atmosphere is both theatrical and intimate, while the drinks are aromatic, beautifully balanced and impeccably crafted.

title: Coquetel Social
bodyText: A vibrant tribute to the styles of Rio and Havana, this bar merges timeless glamour with a hint of nostalgic time travel, evoking an age of slicked-back hair, mellow jazz and unhurried afternoons in hammocks. Celebrated for its captivating ambience, it delivers a lush, immersive escape with a distinctive character.

title: Erlands
bodyText: A charming retro cocktail bar inspired by 1950s and 60s design. Cosy and intimate, it exudes a warm sense of nostalgia, best enjoyed to the sound of soft jazz in the background.

title: Lucy’s Flower Shop
bodyText: A hidden speakeasy concealed behind a flower shop, offering a dark, intimate and perfectly balanced cocktail experience with Nordic flavours. Widely regarded by both guests and industry insiders as Stockholm’s best bar.

title: Facit Bar
bodyText: A vibrant, playful bar in Umeå with a clear focus on Swedish craft spirits. Led by acclaimed bartender Emil Åreng, it blends bold creativity with relaxed northern charm, offering an inviting setting where local flavours take centre stage.

title: Brännerian
bodyText: Located in Stockholm’s historic distillery district, Brännerian celebrates Sweden’s rich spirits heritage and local flavours. Everything here is crafted on a small scale, with creativity, precision and a deep respect for taste.

title: Americain
bodyText: A glamourous cocktail bar with a Riviera touch, where classic drinks are reimagined with modern elegance in a truly luxurious setting.

title: Hernö Gin Bar
bodyText: Hernö Ginbar in Stockholm pays tribute to the award-winning distillery from Härnösand. Here, gin is elevated through imaginative cocktails that showcase distinctive Nordic flavours.

title: Black milk Gastro Cocktailbar
bodyText: This award-winning omakase bar brings together mixology and refined culinary craft, offering pairings that amplify taste and atmosphere in equal measure. The experience unfolds in a space that balances intimacy with a gentle sense of theatre, as the dialogue between kitchen and counter becomes part of the performance.

title: Apropos
bodyText: A contemporary bar where minimalism meets mixology, Apropops is devoted to pure flavours and clean, confident expressions. It is a spot for those who appreciate the craftsmanship behind every cocktail.

title: Stranger
bodyText: A hidden speakeasy accessed by a secret buzzer beneath sister restaurant Tranquilo. The dimly lit, underground bar exudes a vintage charm and is renowned for its expertly crafted Old Fashioneds and prohibition-style cocktails, all crafted with genuine passion.

title: Adamo
bodyText: An elegant hideaway just off Avenyn, where small plates meet refined mixology. An open kitchen and bar create an intimate, lounge-like atmosphere that invites guests to linger over both classic and creative cocktails.

title: Häktet Vaenster
bodyText: Once a detention centre, this striking space has been reimagined as a sleek, minimalist venue with a bistro-style bar and a discreet speakeasy, Vänster. As evening turns to night, the tempo slows and the lights dim, revealing an intimate cocktail lounge that’s perfect for unhurried, late-night sipping.

title: Bar Kusinen
bodyText: In Linköping, this cocktail bar is defined by its spirit of creativity, its commitment to craft and its warm, easy-going character. Drop in for a well-prepared dinner, try the signature cocktails and settle into an atmosphere created simply to make guests feel at ease.

title: Paradiso
bodyText: A vibrant cocktail bar near Mariatorget with a playful, creative spirit and a distinct focus on rum. Expect inventive signature drinks, a lively crowd and a warm, vibrant atmosphere.

title: Gaji
bodyText: Gaji is a polished, effortlessly cool cocktail bar in Malmö, guided by a Korean sensibility and a minimalist philosophy in both its drinks and its design. It offers a refined, understated setting where precision, purity and a sense of calm define the experience.

title: Zigges Garage
bodyText: Tapas and pintxos prepared with care, paired with inventive cocktails mixed with balance and intent. A relaxed, easy-going vibe ties it all together, creating a lively, flavour-led setting where simplicity and creativity meet.

title: Kung Carls Cocktailbar
bodyText: King Carl’s Bar combines turn-of-the-century charm with a modern cocktail sensibility, offering a setting where classic elegance meets contemporary craft. It is a beautifully considered space that feels at once historic and effortlessly relevant.

title: At Six
bodyText: At Six is a place with one restaurant, one bistro, two bars, and a rooftop park, each unique in regard to products, inspiration, and atmosphere, all relentless in their pursuit of culinary excellence.

title: Tak
bodyText: A sleek rooftop destination where Nordic minimalism meets Japanese influence. Guests can enjoy sake and signature cocktails while taking in panoramic views of the city, a year-round favourite for both locals and visitors.

title: Guilty Pleasure
bodyText: In Umeå, the city of birches, this energetic spot blends culinary temptations, good vibes and a touch of disco flair with flavour-led food. It offers a lively interplay of rhythm, colour and comfort, turning an ordinary evening into something playfully memorable.

title: Sju Flaskor
bodyText: A small and intimate bar by the station that prizes quality over quantity. Guests return for its carefully crafted cocktails, warm hospitality and relaxed, unhurried atmosphere, a cosy hideaway where precision and comfort sit naturally side by side.

title: BarBar
bodyText: BarBar is Norrbotten’s only concept bar centered on gin from »GinGin«. Simple but delicious food, great music, exciting guest appearances, and always well-attended evenings all work together to create a uniquely northern atmosphere.

title: Guilty Pleasure
bodyText: A counterpart outpost to Guilty Pleasure in Umeå, carrying the same playful concept and easy-going charm. Expect familiar energy in fresh surroundings, a seamless continuation of the original spirit.

title: Artisan
bodyText: Sweden’s first vermouth bar, an all-day café, restaurant and bar tucked just off Möllevångstorget. Mornings begin with freshly brewed coffee before the mood shifts to expertly crafted vermouth cocktails by evening, all served in a cosy, Southern European–inspired setting.

title: Basta
bodyText: With bold colors, authentic pizza, and handmade pasta, this trattoria grants guests a small Mediterranean holiday. Falun is where the Basta chain began, and the kitchen secured a spot on the 50 Top Pizza list.

title: Bonda Bar & Käk
bodyText: In Östersund—a UNESCO City of Gastronomy—this late-night gastro-bar doubles as an extra living room. Swedish-Greek flavors appear across small plates and main dishes; open Thursday to Saturday.
